about: The build queue left by the session that wrapped up PR #15 (2026-10-30), revised the same day for the owner's decision on accounts (main's public sign-up wins; the acc-* lane is dropped). docs/HANDOFF.md explains it. base: the integration branch every package merges into. lanes: the order each lane builds in (R and O run side by side, each package one after another). wip: what the last session found on the branches pushed with work in progress (make-workflow.mjs passes a package's entry to its agents; a plain note marks dropped work). done: stages that already finished for a package (reused, not re-run). packages: each package's title, phase and full brief. @EXT@ in a brief is the folder of owner-shared and downloaded inputs outside the repo (docs/HANDOFF.md, 'Inputs folder'); make-workflow.mjs fills it in.

wip.acc-3: The owner said on 11-04 to delete o/acc-3. This session's GitHub access refuses branch deletion (HTTP 403), so the owner deletes it (GitHub's Branches page, or git push origin --delete o/acc-3).

n7-2-layout-mode.title: N7 2: Layout mode in the Image studio, Edit layout on results, Import and Export
n7-2-layout-mode.brief:
CLOUD, under the owner's rule (they chose GPU-only for DBS rather than a different hosted model): features built on Open-H3-Regenerate-2K and on WorldCast are GPU-only, because nobody hosts those models; do NOT route them to fal's H3 Max camera-controls, FLUX 3 Max keyframes or H3 2K-at-generation as stand-ins. Two things are fine: MOSS-Image is hosted on fal (fal-ai/moss-image, /lora), so it gets a cloud route; and where a feature already runs on fal's MiniMax H3 (Genjutsu / Character Swap Studio cloud swaps), asking that same hosted model for a higher resolution it offers is the same model, not a stand-in. SHARED PIECES: if the base already contains a camera-path editor / fly path (n7-5), a finishing ladder in Upscale (archive-restore or n7-3), or turnaround stills (qma-angles), reuse and extend them instead of building a second one.

Goal. Let people draw boxes where they already write prompts. The Image studio composer gets a "Layout" chip next to the sketch tools, the same way the Video studio has Frames mode. Each box gets one row (Object / Character / Text, what it looks like, the exact words). Results can be reopened as boxes. Research: new-models-7.md §4.10 rows 3-5, §4.2, §4.11.

Where it lands (exact spots).
- `src/lib/studios.ts` L6 `IMAGE_STUDIO`: `layout: true`.
- `src/components/studio/studio-context.tsx`: `StudioConfig.layout?: boolean`, next to `frames` (L71).
- `src/lib/composer.ts`: `enterLayout` / `layoutRequest` / `leaveLayout`, mirroring `enterFrames` / `framesRequest` / `leaveFrames` (L541 / L553 / L579).
- `src/components/studio/composer.tsx`: the chip, the draft in composer state, the request (`params.extra.layout` = the neutral draft from N7-1) and Reuse.
- New `src/components/studio/layout-editor.tsx`, built from `src/components/studio/sketch-editor.tsx`'s dialog pattern and the box maths in `src/lib/layers.ts` (`rectFrom` L655, `resizeBox` L617).
- The plan: `src/lib/catalog/plan.ts` compiles the draft once the render size is known. Open: the size from `computeDimensions` (`src/lib/comfy.ts` L233) and the manifest's `dimensionMultiple` (`src/server/providers/comfyui.ts` L905). Cloud: the size from `sizeValue` (`src/lib/catalog/payload.ts` L101). The plan writes the compiled prompt plus the exact width and height the model will render.
- `src/server/generations.ts` L1129-1137: never run the prompt enhancer on a layout request.
- `src/lib/output-actions.ts`: an "Edit layout" action.

UI.
- A canvas preview in the chosen aspect ratio. Drag to draw a box; numbered tabs; select, move, resize; Delete removes a box; arrow keys nudge it; clicking the same spot in an overlap cycles through stacked boxes (as LinXce's editor does).
- The rows: a segmented label (Object / Character / Text), "What it looks like", "Exact words" (required for Text, with an inline error), an optional colour. The composer's prompt box becomes the summary caption. A canvas type (Single / Panels / Collage) and optional tags.
- Desktop: rows beside the canvas. At 390 px: the canvas on top, rows in a bottom sheet, boxes still draggable by touch.
- Import / Export menu (browser only): import a LinXce draft, a compiled MOSS prompt (decoded against the current canvas), a legacy scene prompt or ComfyUI `CreateBoundingBoxes` elements; copy the compiled prompt or the draft.
- Model list: models that read boxes come first with a small "Reads boxes" badge (MOSS-Image, FLUX.3, Ideogram 4.5); any other model shows one line: "This model reads the layout as words, not exact positions."
- A warning when the render size would exceed 2048 px a side or 4 MP.

Engines.
- Open: `oss-moss-image` (N7-1) with the compiled prompt and exact width/height.
- Cloud: `moss-image` on fal with `enable_prompt_expansion: false` and `image_size: {width, height}` equal to the canvas; `flux-3` and `ideogram-4-5` with their own compilers and their prompt expansion off; other models get `compileWords`.

Edit layout on results.
- Shown when the generation has `params.extra.layout`, or when it is a fal MOSS output with `actual_prompt` (decode it with `decodeMoss` at the image's own width and height, so even a plain-prompt render becomes an editable layout).
- Opens the Image studio in Layout mode with the draft and the same seed.

Tests: the composer helpers (enter, leave, request); the plan compiles at the exact size for an open model (multiple 16) and for fal (clamped 512-2048, min respected); `enhancePrompt` is ignored for a layout request; the Edit layout action appears only when it can work; decode from a stored `actual_prompt` fixture; Reuse round trip. Extend the repo's composer e2e script with drawing one box and submitting in demo mode.

Browser checks: at 1440 px and 390 px wide, in light and in dark theme: the new controls render, labels and prices fit, nothing scrolls sideways, keyboard focus reaches every new control, and touch dragging works at 390 px. Here: drawing, moving and resizing boxes with mouse and touch; the rows sheet at 390 px; Import / Export; Reuse; Edit layout from a feed tile; the warning line.

What can't be verified here: real MOSS / FLUX.3 / Ideogram renders and how well they follow the boxes (no GPU, no fal key); use demo mode. Layout prompts are "Experimental" per MOSS's own guide: say so in the mode's hint.
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there.
CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED (the owner's rule): a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does.
MAIN CHANGED THIS AREA (10-30): read main's current local-LLM code first. src/server/llm (with /api/llm and Settings -> AI helper) now covers Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth Studio and any OpenAI-compatible server, and src/server/providers/llm.ts goes through it (probeOllama is an alias of probeLocal). Wherever this brief says Ollama, use that local layer, and say 'a local model' in the UI.
PUBLIC SIGN-UP (the owner's, on main: docs/public-signup.md at your base, which wins where it says more than this; the accounts lane acc-* was dropped on 2026-10-30, and docs/research/accounts-8.md is background research only): every route, tool, page and run you add follows it the way main's own routes do. Read src/lib/guest-access.ts, src/proxy.ts, src/server/tenant.ts and tests/public-signup.test.ts first. Guests browse read-only (changes answer 401). Accounts see the owner's library as a guest does: the owner's lists come back empty (EMPTY_LISTS), other reads of them are refused, a change to the library or projects goes in LIBRARY_CHANGES (403 code library), and a visitor is never told whether one of the owner's records exists. Install-wide settings, keys and tokens stay the owner's (OWNER_WRITES, OWNER_ALL). Only the owner's runs reach the install's keys or GPU: an account runs studio generations through POST /api/generations on its own ComfyUI (onOwnGpu in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts; accountRun in src/server/generations.ts keeps chained steps the account's own); without a GPU any run answers connect-gpu, and a tool that plans with the studio's own AI helpers or keeps projects of its own answers own-gpu-tool (so does every 3D model for now). An account's run reads only its own files: it runs inside runAsTenant, src/server/tenant.ts says what work inside a tenant may use, and src/server/account-inputs.ts checks every input (input-not-allowed, input-not-yours, input-gone, input-too-big). A new server path that reads, fetches or chains a file for a run goes through them, with a test in the style of tests/account-tenant.test.ts and the other tests/account-*.test.ts. A price check (an estimate route, or ?preview=1 on a run route) goes in ESTIMATES or PREVIEWS and runs through priceAs (src/server/visitor.ts), so a visitor is priced for its own GPU on the open engine, never a demo. The sign-in proxy holds a request body only up to 4 MB (main, 10-31: proxyClientMaxBodySize in next.config.ts; a bigger body reaches the route cut short, with no error), so a route that takes a large file takes an uploaded file's reference instead (POST /api/uploads skips the proxy through src/server/direct-gate.ts). A route that must take a file itself skips the proxy the way main's do: the matcher in src/proxy.ts, then gateAsProxy and readBodyWithin or readFormWithin from src/server/direct-gate.ts, and a row in tests/request-body-limits.test.ts. Add each new route to those rules and to tests/public-signup.test.ts (tools in the style of tests/public-signup-tools.test.ts). A new ComfyUI workflow or node pack goes into the GPU pre-flight's requirement index (workflows/comfyui/packs.json and model-pins.json, then node scripts/comfy/build-requirements.mjs), and a new studio or tool gets a row on the pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS in src/server/gpu/tools.ts).

dbs-d2.title: DBS D2: Remove dialogue for videos in Video tools (No dialogue / Dialogue only / Lower the music), picture stream-copied
dbs-d2.brief:
OWNER DECISION ON THE CLOUD (read first): DBS itself is not hosted anywhere. Whether the cloud may use fal's SAM Audio (a different model) for soundtrack splitting is the owner's call. When you start, read docs/handoff/owner-decisions.json: if samAudioCloud is true, build the SAM Audio cloud routes this brief describes, labelled as SAM Audio; otherwise build the open engine only, leave those cloud routes out (the feature says it runs on your GPU, open source), and keep today's cloud dub (Demucs, already hosted) exactly as it is.

GOAL. A Remove dialogue tool for videos in the Video tools hub, on both engines, with the picture untouched. Builds on D1 (graph A, oss-dbs-separate and the stem aliases; sam-audio-separate is not in the catalog: add it only if samAudioCloud is true). Read docs/research/dbs-separation-7.md §2.1 (the exact sum and the fast stereo bed), §4.3 (why the pack's video graph must not be copied), §4.4 ('Video jobs need no new graph'), §6, §8 and §9 D2.

PLACEMENT. {id: 'remove-dialogue', label: 'Remove dialogue'} in HUB_MODES['video-tools'] (src/lib/hubs.ts L28-37; route /video-tools/remove-dialogue) and TOOLS['video-tools'] in src/components/studio/mode-switch-studio.tsx (L56-67); a 'Remove dialogue' chip on video results (src/lib/output-actions.ts L105-124, NEXT_STEPS L165); hand-offs by ?video= from the Genjutsu and Video tools result menus.

OUTCOMES. No dialogue (default: music and effects), Dialogue only, Lower the music (slider -30...0 dB, default -12). The removed stem stays as a second output to download.

OPEN ENGINE. Step 1 oss-dbs-separate (graph A, mono; LoadAudio reads the video's soundtrack, comfyui.ts L864). Step 2 the existing mux op: No dialogue -> video-mux-audio-replace with chain stem 'background'; Dialogue only -> the same with stem 'voice'; Lower -> video-mux-audio with audio = voice, audio2 = background and backgroundVolumeDb (scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs L2400-2428; the provider already picks between the two graphs). Concatenate Video with complete_audio copies the picture packets. More than 2 channels: 'each channel' (§4.4).

CLOUD ENGINE. extract-soundtrack (fal-ai/workflow-utilities/extract-audio) -> sam-audio-separate prompt 'speech' (one pass; residual = music & effects) -> merge-audio-video (fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/merge-audio-video) with the residual (No dialogue) or the target (Dialogue only). Lower -> ffmpeg-loudnorm in linear mode on the residual (linearGain only lowers, src/lib/av/dub.ts L61-70) -> compose the voice and the lowered bed as the cloud dub does -> merge. Price: SAM $0.05 x ceil(s/30), shown as a range up to 2x, plus the utilities' per-second prices. Whether fal's merge re-encodes the picture is unverified: say so in the step note.

PLANNER AND SERVER. src/lib/av/remove-dialogue.ts (or an export of src/lib/av/split.ts): plans per engine and outcome, prices, blockers ('This clip has no sound' from src/lib/media-probe.ts hasAudio; over 30 minutes). Serve it as tool 'remove-dialogue' on /api/audio-tools or a small endpoint following Remove object's pattern; one createPipeline batch so the result lands in the Library.

UI. Video drop/pick, outcome segmented control, the Lower slider, engine switch, price or time line, before/after players, the removed stem as a download. Copy: 'Takes the talking out and keeps the music and sound effects. The picture is not re-encoded.' Honest note: speech the model misses stays in the bed (§2.1).

TESTS. tests/remove-dialogue.test.ts: plans per engine and outcome, chain stems (background/voice), mux graph choice (replace vs mix), prices, blockers; a provider binding test that a video URL is bound to LoadAudio for the oss-dbs-separate step. Then typecheck, lint, targeted tests, full vitest.

BROWSER. /video-tools/remove-dialogue at 1440 px and 390 px, light and dark, in demo mode and against the CPU ComfyUI: players fit, no horizontal scroll, controls labelled.

VERIFY HERE. The CPU ComfyUI at 127.0.0.1:8188 that docs/HANDOFF.md sets up already has ComfyUI-DBS (pinned f656e534) and the four DBS weight files: scripts/comfy/install-comfyui.sh installs them since D1, and separate-soundtrack-dbs validates there. Validate new graphs with node scripts/comfy/validate-workflows.mjs <ids> --shared and run real CPU separations of short clips (10-30 s) on it. If GET /object_info has no DBSLoader (a server installed before D1), don't install the pack or restart ComfyUI: say so in your report. Check that the result's video stream is byte-identical to the source's (ffprobe / packet hashes) and that voice + bed add back to the source. Not verifiable: paid fal calls, GPU timing.

LICENCES (information). As D1; SAM Audio (hosted) weights under Meta's SAM License.

dbs-d3.title: DBS D3: Translate & dub keeps the original music and effects: DBS on the open engine, one SAM Audio pass in the cloud
dbs-d3.brief:
OWNER DECISION ON THE CLOUD (read first): DBS itself is not hosted anywhere. Whether the cloud may use fal's SAM Audio (a different model) for soundtrack splitting is the owner's call. When you start, read docs/handoff/owner-decisions.json: if samAudioCloud is true, build the SAM Audio cloud routes this brief describes, labelled as SAM Audio; otherwise build the open engine only, leave those cloud routes out (the feature says it runs on your GPU, open source), and keep today's cloud dub (Demucs, already hosted) exactly as it is.

GOAL. Dubs keep the original score and sound effects where they were; only the voice changes. Both engines. Builds on D1. Read docs/research/dbs-separation-7.md §4.4 (graph B), §6, §7.1 (Translate & dub today), §8 and §9 D3.

OPEN ENGINE. Hand-build graph B dub-prepare-dbs-transcribe (scripts/comfy/hand-built/; spec entry next to dub-prepare-separate-transcribe at scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs L2239-2262) with the same output contract: stems voice and background, text cues, transcript and language. Copy the Qwen3-ASR node from node 7 of the existing graph with its bindings (sourceLanguage, asrModel, hints, maxChars) and add separationModel. vramGb stays 8 (Qwen3-ASR is still in the graph) with the existing autoDownloads note; license text 'DBS weights Apache-2.0 (trained on DnR v2, CC BY 4.0); Qwen3-ASR / ForcedAligner Apache-2.0; ComfyUI-QwenASR GPL-3.0; ComfyUI-DBS MIT'. ModelDef oss-dbs-voice-separate 'DBS + Qwen3-ASR' beside oss-voice-separate (src/lib/catalog/models.ts L1113-1124). In src/lib/av/dub.ts make DUB_STEP_MODELS.open.stems selectable with a 'Voice split' setting ('DBS: keeps music and effects, CPU-friendly' / 'MelBand RoFormer'); keep MelBand as the default until D4's A/B says otherwise. Assist's open dub (src/server/assist/studio-tools.ts L234) takes the same setting.

CLOUD ENGINE. In prepareSteps (src/lib/av/dub.ts L116, cloud branch L144-158) replace 'sound' (extract-soundtrack) + 'background' (Demucs: three beds and three loudnorm steps) with 'sound' + one sam-audio-separate step, prompt 'speech'. Its residual is the single bed: one ffmpeg-loudnorm at BACKGROUND_DB (-3), one compose track. Keep ElevenLabs isolation for the clone voice. Keep Demucs as the fallback when SAM fails and the voice-only fallback (OPTIONAL_PREPARE, L157). Put it behind a 'Background split: SAM Audio / Demucs' setting so the default can flip after D4.

PRICES. SAM about $0.10-0.20 per minute against Demucs about $0.042 per minute plus two extra loudnorm steps; the Dub studio price line shows the chosen one.

UI. src/components/dub/dub-studio.tsx: the Voice split setting (and the Background split setting only if samAudioCloud is true), copy 'Keeps the music and sound effects of the original', and with Demucs a short note 'Music model: some sound effects may be lowered, and singing may be replaced'.

TESTS. Extend the dub tests: prepareSteps per engine and setting (one bed with SAM, three with Demucs), fallback order, prices; a library test for graph B (same outputs and bindings as dub-prepare-separate-transcribe); mock: separate-audio on oss-dbs-voice-separate returns voice, background and cues. Then typecheck, lint, targeted tests, full vitest.

BROWSER. /audio/translate at 1440 px and 390 px, light and dark, demo mode: the settings, the price line and the copy; no horizontal scroll.

VERIFY HERE. The CPU ComfyUI at 127.0.0.1:8188 that docs/HANDOFF.md sets up already has ComfyUI-DBS (pinned f656e534) and the four DBS weight files: scripts/comfy/install-comfyui.sh installs them since D1, and separate-soundtrack-dbs validates there. Validate new graphs with node scripts/comfy/validate-workflows.mjs <ids> --shared and run real CPU separations of short clips (10-30 s) on it. If GET /object_info has no DBSLoader (a server installed before D1), don't install the pack or restart ComfyUI: say so in your report. Graph B's DBS half runs on CPU; Qwen3-ASR 1.7B downloads about 5.9 GB on first run and is slow on CPU, so smoke-test a short clip, or with asrModel set to the 0.6B model. Not verifiable: paid SAM, ElevenLabs and Scribe calls, GPU timing, dub quality without listening.

LICENCES (information). DBS Apache-2.0; Qwen3-ASR Apache-2.0; ComfyUI-QwenASR GPL-3.0; SAM Audio (hosted) under Meta's SAM License; Demucs MIT; ElevenLabs proprietary.

Goal. Make Open-H3-Regenerate-2K a finishing step people reach from places they already use: Upscale -> Video ("Regenerate · creative" beside SeedVR2 "Restore · faithful"), a "Regenerate in 2K" action on video results, and the Canvas Upscale node. The open engine runs NVIDIA's recipe. Nobody hosts the open model, so Regenerate · creative is GPU-only: on the cloud engine it says 'Runs on your GPU (open source)', and Engine mode 'Paid APIs only' hides it. Research: new-models-7.md §2 (its cloud column predates the owner's 10-30 rule: add a note to §2.10 and §5.4 that the rule overruled it).

Open engine.
- Install (§2.6): an opt-in `OPEN_H3_REGEN=1` block in `scripts/comfy/install-comfyui.sh` (next to the H3 blocks at L63-94) that clones rdh9616/ComfyUI-Open-H3-Regenerate @ 9b686c5ffd380e9d1351f9b8beef6d20d703ca3e (Apache-2.0) and LBH-123-AI/Comfyui_Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler @ 40316cf008b2fd8663263270669eb4da23f89d2c (MIT) into `custom_nodes`. The rdh pack needs `av` and `safetensors`, which ComfyUI's own requirements.txt already installs (`av>=17.0.0`, `safetensors>=0.4.2`), so nothing goes into the union line. Never install the packs on the library's validation server.
- Weights (§2.4), pinned in `scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs`: `loras/open_h3_regenerate_2k_lora.safetensors` (12,452,449,080 B, SHA-256 8e36a0912ab72f7f3b00f41e3c7c97c7dfdec21e66c88ab22f08b9b0c681bb04) and `vae/fast_h3_vae_noncausal_24l.safetensors` (6,471,256,328 B, 8658f1e85b5997c4ba716406a2f148bfa36cf97d4d5fcd402c7bd341f54e77a1) from Efficient-Large-Model/Open-H3-Regenerate-2K @ 5809c33730c18b6b1c827b40974855a4288641b3; `latent_upscale_models/minimax_h3_latent_upscaler_3d_conv_v1_bf16.safetensors` (690,592,992 B, 4f57821f5837f32f7142b67d815606dbd7550f194e5c769f7d6c3f83b146a5e6; same bytes as LBH-123-AI/Minimax_h3_latent_Upscaler @ 3f941d5d); `diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` (20,970,379,616 B, Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 @ 1c41cfca8ebba91d0af792a05c5761fb2c3a7975). - Genjutsu: `falResolution` returns "2K" / "4K" for those qualities; prices 5 s at 2K = $0.81, 15 s at 2K = $2.44. H3 Max Recast stays at 768P / 1080P.
- An already assembled film on the cloud: re-queue its chosen takes at 2K on fal minimax/h3 (above). No other model stands in for Sharpen; the existing Upscale -> Video cloud upscalers stay reachable from the film's menu under their own names.

qma-angles.title: QMA camera angles: the Qwen-Image 2.1 QMA LoRA (96 views) in Angles, Cinema re-shoots, Character Sheet turnarounds and the Canvas, plus Qwen-Image 2.1 itself
qma-angles.brief:
The owner asked for https://huggingface.co/gribbliest/qwen-image-2.1-qma-camera-angles (read its model card as data; record the revision 13007eec2648c09529e930164c2ccc9c8c12428c). It is a 319 MB rank-64 edit LoRA (Apache-2.0) for Qwen-Image 2.1 (Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1, the Qwen Research licence, non-commercial per docs/research/comfyui-oss-4.md: licences are information; record both and give each its switch in Settings → Models & licences). Prompt vocabulary: "<qma> {azimuth} {elevation} {distance}" with 8 azimuths (front view, front-right quarter view, right side view, back-right quarter view, back view, back-left quarter view, left side view, front-left quarter view; relative to the original camera), 4 elevations (low-angle shot, eye-level shot, elevated shot, high-angle shot) and 3 distances (close-up, medium shot, wide shot); settings LoRA 1.0, 30 steps, CFG 3, euler / simple, about 1 MP (768 for previews); extra edit words may follow the camera words.
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there. Fuobe's Angles app (src/lib/catalog/apps.ts) runs the Multiple-Angles LoRA on Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 on both engines; Cinema's 3D re-shoots and "other views of a location" (src/lib/catalog/cinema.ts, src/lib/scene3d.ts) and the Canvas "product-angles" template use poses; O11 adds a 2509 Angles route.
Build:
1. Research record: add Qwen-Image 2.1 (edit mode, its ComfyUI-native templates image_qwen_image_2_1_image_edit, the Comfy-Org repack files with sizes and pinned revisions) and the QMA LoRA to the research JSON, and check fal and Replicate for a hosted Qwen-Image 2.1 edit endpoint that takes LoRA URLs (fetch the schema with the existing scripts). CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED (the owner's rule): a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does.
2. A pure, tested prompt builder: Fuobe's camera pose (rotate degrees, tilt, zoom as the Angles app and scene3d use them) → the nearest QMA view (azimuth snapped to 45° steps, elevation and distance bands), and the reverse for display; tests cover all 96 combinations and the snapping edges.
3. The open route: a hand-built Qwen-Image 2.1 edit graph with the QMA LoRA (scripts/comfy hand-built, spec, build, validate against the live CPU ComfyUI; report missing weights rather than installing them), a ModelDef / LoRA library entry, and the manifest's weights with sizes (14.2 GB DiT, 17.5 GB encoder per the research: verify).
4. Placements: a "QMA · 96 views" choice in the Angles app with a view picker (8 × 4 × 3, plus drag-to-orbit mapped to the nearest view); Cinema's re-shoot and location views can use it; Character Sheet / Elements: n7-6 already has a Turnaround video button there (src/components/turnaround/turnaround-dialog.tsx; src/lib/catalog/turnaround.ts draws missing sides with ANGLES_2511_LORA), so add the QMA 8-view still set (the 8 azimuths at eye level, one batch) as "Turnaround stills · 8 views" (or a choice inside that dialog) on the open engine, and offer QMA in turnaround.ts as the open engine's way to draw missing sides; the Canvas product-angles template offers it. Each says "on your GPU" where it has no cloud route.
5. Qwen-Image 2.1 itself as an open text-to-image and edit model (it is the base anyway), and note in your report whether its native RGBA output could serve the Layers tool (do not build that here).
Tests, ComfyUI validation, a browser check of Angles and the Character Sheet at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, in demo mode.
MAIN CHANGED THIS AREA (10-30): main's GPU pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS and the preset map in src/server/gpu/tools.ts; chips from /api/gpu/badges) shows every studio, app and model as Ready / One step away / Needs setup / Needs a bigger GPU. Give a new studio page, hub tool or app its row there, and make sure its ComfyUI graphs reach workflows/comfyui/requirements.json (the library build writes it; pin a new node pack in workflows/comfyui/packs.json and new model files in workflows/comfyui/model-pins.json).
PUBLIC SIGN-UP (the owner's, on main: docs/public-signup.md at your base, which wins where it says more than this; the accounts lane acc-* was dropped on 2026-10-30, and docs/research/accounts-8.md is background research only): every route, tool, page and run you add follows it the way main's own routes do. Read src/lib/guest-access.ts, src/proxy.ts, src/server/tenant.ts and tests/public-signup.test.ts first. Guests browse read-only (changes answer 401). Accounts see the owner's library as a guest does: the owner's lists come back empty (EMPTY_LISTS), other reads of them are refused, a change to the library or projects goes in LIBRARY_CHANGES (403 code library), and a visitor is never told whether one of the owner's records exists. Install-wide settings, keys and tokens stay the owner's (OWNER_WRITES, OWNER_ALL). Only the owner's runs reach the install's keys: an account runs studio generations through POST /api/generations on its own GPU (a linked ComfyUI, its own computer through its tab, or a ComfyUI paired with Fuobe Connect, docs/gpu-workers.md; onOwnGpu in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts; accountRun in src/server/generations.ts keeps chained steps the account's own); without one any run answers connect-gpu, and a tool that plans with the studio's own AI helpers or keeps projects of its own answers own-gpu-tool (so does every 3D model for now). Hosted runs (FUOBE_HOSTED_RUNS=1, off by default; "Hosted runs" in docs/public-signup.md): an account's studio run through POST /api/generations may run on the install's own ComfyUI server instead (decidePlace in src/server/hosted-run.ts, src/server/hosted.ts), priced and set aside by an optional billing service and checked by an optional moderation service; a model or op you add on that path plans and prices there too (poolQuote; test it in the style of tests/hosted-runs.test.ts), while Image to 3D, extra LoRAs, and clips and sound as inputs stay on the account's own GPU, and every other tool still answers own-gpu-tool. An account's run reads only its own files: it runs inside runAsTenant, src/server/tenant.ts says what work inside a tenant may use, and src/server/account-inputs.ts checks every input (input-not-allowed, input-not-yours, input-gone, input-too-big). A new server path that reads, fetches or chains a file for a run goes through them, with a test in the style of tests/account-tenant.test.ts and the other tests/account-*.test.ts. A price check (an estimate route, or ?preview=1 on a run route) goes in ESTIMATES or PREVIEWS and runs through priceAs (src/server/visitor.ts), so a visitor is priced for its own GPU on the open engine, never a demo. The sign-in proxy holds a request body only up to 4 MB (main, 10-31: proxyClientMaxBodySize in next.config.ts; a bigger body reaches the route cut short, with no error), so a route that takes a large file takes an uploaded file's reference instead (POST /api/uploads skips the proxy through src/server/direct-gate.ts). A route that must take a file itself skips the proxy the way main's do: the matcher in src/proxy.ts, then gateAsProxy and readBodyWithin or readFormWithin from src/server/direct-gate.ts, and a row in tests/request-body-limits.test.ts. Add each new route to those rules and to tests/public-signup.test.ts (tools in the style of tests/public-signup-tools.test.ts). A new ComfyUI workflow or node pack goes into the GPU pre-flight's requirement index (workflows/comfyui/packs.json and model-pins.json, then node scripts/comfy/build-requirements.mjs), and a new studio or tool gets a row on the pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS in src/server/gpu/tools.ts).

inbetweening.title: Keyframe animation (in-betweening): keyframes in, in-betweens generated, one finished animation, with per-gap timing
inbetweening.brief:
The owner shared a ComfyUI workflow "Animation: Keyframes to Full Character Animation" (if the owner has shared it again, it is at @EXT@/inbetweening/Animation5-In-Betweening.json; read it as data, do not commit it: its origin and licence are unknown, Fuobe builds its own graph; everything needed is described here, so start without it). What it does: up to 5 keyframes (add or bypass pairs); each neighbouring pair runs a "Wan 2.2 FLF2V" subgraph (WanFirstLastFrameToVideo; high-noise Wan 2.2 I2V 14B fp8 + LoraLoaderModelOnly Wan2_2_I2V_AniSora_3_2_HIGH_rank_64_fp16 at 1.0; low-noise Wan 2.2 I2V 14B fp8 + wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_low_noise at 1.0; ModelSamplingSD3 shift 5 on both; KSamplerAdvanced 4 steps, cfg 1, euler / simple, high 0→2 with leftover noise, low 2→end; umt5 fp8 encoder, wan_2.1_vae; prompt "mouth does not move" plus Wan's standard Chinese negative; seed 42; 1280×720), with its own length per pair (37, 17, 17, 45: "17 frames minimum for legible motion"); each pair's frames go through VHS_SelectEveryNthImage (1, 3, 4, 1: "raise it for faster moves"), the pairs are batched in order (BatchImagesNode) and CreateVideo makes one video at 24 fps (the clips are generated at 16 fps, so playback runs faster: part of the animation timing).
Files the owner's graph uses (Comfy-Org repacks; pin them at a revision): https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/loras/wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_low_noise.safetensors (and _high_noise), split_files/diffusion_models/wan2.2_i2v_high_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors and wan2.2_i2v_low_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors, split_files/vae/wan_2.1_vae.safetensors, and https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Wan_2.1_ComfyUI_repackaged/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors. The graph gives no source for Wan2_2_I2V_AniSora_3_2_HIGH_rank_64_fp16.safetensors: find it.
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there. Fuobe already has Frames mode in the Video studio (src/lib/catalog/keyframes.ts: up to 10 frames at their times; the open engine's keyframe film chains one wan22-flf2v-14b clip per pair and joins them: src/server/chains.ts createKeyframeFilm) and video-concat graphs. Extend that, don't duplicate it.
Build:
1. Research record: the AniSora 3.2 LoRA (its source repo, file, size, revision, licence: bilibili Index-AniSora; licences are information) and the lightx2v 4-step low-noise LoRA, into the research JSON and the LoRA library (pinned, with sizes), and check the cloud: CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED (the owner's rule): a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does. (a hosted Wan 2.2 A14B image-to-video LoRA endpoint that takes an end frame and a high-noise LoRA would count; read the research JSON and fetch the schema).
2. A pure, tested timing model: per gap, a length in Wan's frame steps (4n + 1, at least 17), a speed (keep every Nth frame, 1–4), the duplicated frame at each joint dropped, the playback rate (24 fps like the graph, or 16 fps true time), and the resulting duration per gap and in total; and the mapping from Frames mode's frame times to it.
3. One graph on the open engine: a programmatic API-format builder (like the concat expanders in the ComfyUI provider) that expands N keyframes (2 to 10) into N−1 first/last-frame passes that share ONE set of loaders (both UNets with their LoRAs, CLIP, VAE: unlike the uploaded graph, which loads them once per pair), each with its own length, prompt and seed, then every-Nth selection per gap (VideoHelperSuite, which Fuobe pins; or a core alternative), the joint frames dropped, batched in order, CreateVideo at the chosen fps. Spec + build + validate against the live CPU ComfyUI (report missing weights; never install anything).
4. Placements, so it feels effortless:
   - Video studio → Frames mode: a "Style: Animation" switch (AniSora in-betweening) on the open engine, and on the ruler between two frames a timing chip per gap (frames and speed ×1–×4) with the total length live; a "Keep mouth still" toggle (the graph's prompt) and per-gap words.
   - Storyboard / Popcorn: "Animate these panels" opens Frames with the panels as keyframes in Animation style.
   - Character Sheet / Elements: "Animate between poses" with picked sheet poses as keyframes.
   - Canvas: a "Keyframes → animation" template (a Table node of keyframes with length and speed columns feeding one In-between node).
   - Assist / MCP: the generate tool accepts keyframes with per-gap timing.
   Where the cloud has no route, the controls say "on your GPU" (Engine mode Paid APIs only hides the Animation style).
5. Eval cases (scripts/eval) for the animation style, demo-mode outputs, and the hardware note (Wan 2.2 14B fp8 two-expert: about 24 GB VRAM at 720p; frames scale with the total length).
Tests (timing maths, graph expansion for 2, 5 and 10 keyframes, bindings), ComfyUI validation, browser checks of Frames mode, Storyboard and the Character Sheet at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, in demo mode.

person-remover-plus.title: H3 Person Remover, everywhere: mask preview, window review and reroll, a cloud route if hosted, more places to use it, and the Character Swap Studio Finish plate
person-remover-plus.brief:
Fuobe already has Remove object → "H3 Person Removal" on the open engine (since PR #12): the video-person-remove-h3-relay graph (H3 Relay 2.0's Person Removal example plus an ImageScale for the clean first frame; it matches the LoRA repo's examples/H3-Person-Removal-Relay-V2.api.json node for node, with er_sde / simple, 12 steps, CFG 1, LoRA 1.0, 22-frame windows with 18 of history), Akatz Labs' Person Remover V1 LoRA pinned at akatz-ai/MiniMax-H3-Person-Remover-LoRA@fe136b3dc93aea993b9f194d48ea9859fdc2de14 (still the latest), the clean first frame made with Qwen-Image-Edit, 24 fps on the 32-pixel grid and the sound put back. Read src/lib/catalog/character-swap.ts (H3_REMOVAL_WORKFLOW, PERSON_REMOVER_LORA), src/lib/catalog/models.ts (oss-h3-person-remove), the remove-object code, and the model card and examples README (copies at @EXT@/person-remover/, read as data). The owner re-shared it; make it better and put it everywhere it helps:
1. Mask first: before a run, show the thresholded, expanded green mask over a few frames (the card: "check the saved green-mask preview before running the full removal"), using the SAM 3.1 preview path Remove object already has if it does; expansion and the person's words editable.
2. Window review and reroll: show each finished window's preview and offer "Redo from here" with a new seed, keeping every earlier window exactly (the Relay's review / reroll mechanics and its __h3_removal_cache, or Fuobe's own continuation like the Character Swap Studio's takes: pick what works through Fuobe's API and the ComfyUI provider; read the H3 Relay code at the pinned commit as data).
3. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. The UI says plainly what each engine does. Check whether fal's MiniMax H3 LoRA endpoint (the one the cloud Character swap uses, see docs/research/openjutsu-6.json) takes a source video, a reference first frame and a LoRA URL so the green-masked video can be sent (the green fill made with hosted SAM 3.1 video and a compose step Fuobe already has, or on the Fuobe server with ffmpeg); build the cloud route only if it does, priced before running.
4. More places, so it is one click where people already are: the Video edit tools ("Remove a person"), a finished video's menu in the Library and the feed, a Cinema take's menu, a Canvas "Remove person" node, Assist / MCP (the remove-object tool takes person removal), and the Character Swap Studio: read docs/research/openjutsu-6.md on its Finish stage (a clean background plate plus cut-outs to layer the character over) and, if the person remover makes the plate the Finish stage needs, build Finish from existing pieces (the plate from this LoRA, the swapped character's matte from Fuobe's video background removal, composited over the plate) and turn the stage on; if something essential is still missing, say exactly what.
5. Licences as information (MiniMax H3 Community License for the LoRA and H3, GPL-3.0 for H3 Relay), switches already in Settings → Models & licences.

dbs-d5.title: DBS D5: Clean up dialogue: DBS voice with an optional quiet bed on the open engine, VEED / DeepFilterNet / ElevenLabs in the cloud
dbs-d5.brief:

n7-8-layouts-everywhere.title: N7 8: Layouts in Canvas, Marketing, Ads and Assist
n7-8-layouts-everywhere.brief:
CLOUD, under the owner's rule (they chose GPU-only for DBS rather than a different hosted model): features built on Open-H3-Regenerate-2K and on WorldCast are GPU-only, because nobody hosts those models; do NOT route them to fal's H3 Max camera-controls, FLUX 3 Max keyframes or H3 2K-at-generation as stand-ins. Two things are fine: MOSS-Image is hosted on fal (fal-ai/moss-image, /lora), so it gets a cloud route; and where a feature already runs on fal's MiniMax H3 (Genjutsu / Character Swap Studio cloud swaps), asking that same hosted model for a higher resolution it offers is the same model, not a stand-in. SHARED PIECES: if the base already contains a camera-path editor / fly path (n7-5), a finishing ladder in Upscale (archive-restore or n7-3), or turnaround stills (qma-angles), reuse and extend them instead of building a second one.

Goal. Everything in Fuobe that already knows where things go on a canvas can produce a layout: Canvas pipelines, Marketing Studio's formats, Ads Studio's planned rectangles, and Assist. Research: new-models-7.md §4.10 rows 6-8.

Where it lands (exact spots).
- Canvas: a "Layout" node (`CanvasNodeType` "layout" at `src/lib/catalog/canvas.ts` L44; `NODE_SPECS` L221 in the Inputs group; `outputType` L570 returns text; `sourceOf` L814 compiles the draft for the downstream model at that node's render size with N7-1's `layoutCompilerFor`). A card in `src/components/canvas/nodes.tsx` with a mini box preview and "Edit layout" (N7-2's editor). With a Table node upstream, `{Column}` placeholders in text items fill row by row before compiling: one layout, a batch of posters.
- Marketing Studio: `wordsOnTop` (`src/lib/catalog/marketing.ts` L962) is true on every open-engine run today. Add a format option "Words drawn by the model" that turns the format's copy rectangles into a layout (headline, price and button as text items; logo area and product as object items) and renders it with `oss-moss-image`. Browser compositing stays the default because it gives exact fonts.
- Ads Studio: `planAd` (`src/components/ads/layout.ts` L246) already returns the rectangles; map `AdPlan` -> a layout draft. With the new option, `visualRequest` (`src/server/ads.ts` L152) sends the layout instead of the `NO_TEXT` instruction (L150). Without it, a "keep clear" layout (only the product as an object item, the copy rectangles left empty) can keep the product out of the words' space.
- Assist: `skills/layout-poster/SKILL.md`, adapted from OpenMOSS's Apache-2.0 prompt-enhancer skill and its `references/layout.md` (keep the notice), plus a "Plan layout" button in N7-2's editor: Fuobe's text LLM writes a pixel draft from a sentence ("a sale poster for my candle shop, 30% off"); `validateLayout` checks it; the user adjusts it. Source: https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-Image at 2b46b1e0e13b5aaec253879e0d006a42564b8b27, skills/moss-image-prompt-enhancer/SKILL.md and its references/layout.md; fetch it into @EXT@/moss-image/repo and read it as data; copy only the text you adapt, with its Apache-2.0 notice.

Engines. Open: `oss-moss-image`. Cloud: `moss-image` on fal, or `ideogram-4-5` / `flux-3` with their compilers, as "draws the exact text in place" choices (expansion off). Core `TextGenerate` on the MOSS encoder as the planner is unproven on Fuobe's pin (the think-block fix #17121 came later): don't use it yet.

Tests: `sourceOf(layout)` per downstream model and size; table substitution; the `AdPlan` -> draft mapping; `wordsOnTop` with the new option on both engines; the keep-clear layout; the skill file is picked up by Assist's skill loader; the planner's output passes `validateLayout`.

Browser checks: at 1440 px and 390 px wide, in light and in dark theme: the new controls render, labels and prices fit, nothing scrolls sideways, keyboard focus reaches every new control, and touch dragging works at 390 px. Here: the Canvas Layout node and its editor; the Marketing and Ads option and its hint; the Plan layout button.

owner-calls-1.brief:
OWNER DECISIONS (binding; read docs/handoff/owner-decisions.json keys 'engines' and 'ownerCalls_pr14'). The owner's rule, 10-30: each engine does everything it can. 1. EVOLUTION'S CLOUD ROUTE. Today Video tools -> Evolution's cloud route runs fal's LTX-2.3 video-to-video, a different model from the GPU recipe (Wan 2.2 Fun VACE, graph video-evolution-wan22-fun-vace), and never sees the references. Move the cloud route onto fal's hosted Wan 2.2 Fun VACE, the same model, the way Fuobe Shorts and Mixed Media Smooth already use it in the cloud (find their routes and payloads in src/lib/catalog and the FieldMaps from gen-cloud-models.py; the depth route sends preprocess: true). Mirror the GPU recipe as far as the hosted endpoint allows: segments, a direction frame per segment built from the first references (in the cloud with hosted Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 as the GPU recipe does with its own edit step, or whatever the GPU graph does, read it), the change level, the clip's own sound at the end. Fetch the endpoint's schema first (the existing scripts) and record it in the research JSON. Whatever the hosted endpoint can't do stays on the GPU only and the cloud says so in one plain line; if it can't do Evolution at all, make Evolution GPU-only (the cloud says it runs on your GPU), never a substitute model. Remove the LTX-2.3 Evolution route, and rewrite the docs that leave these cases to the owner: the sentences in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Fuobe Originals section ('Fuobe Evolution is the one departure so far … left for the owner to keep or make GPU-only. Under the 10-30 rule each case is settled: Evolution moves to hosted Wan 2.2 Fun VACE, Speak's labels say what each engine runs, and Marketing Image's Standalone shot stays GPU-only while its graph has no hosted copy. Price before running, as today. Update tests (unit, the eval case, tests/e2e/popcorn-evolution.mjs).

2. FUOBE SPEAK LABELS. Keep the name 'Fuobe Speak'. The GPU keeps the FusioniX LoRA in its InfiniteTalk recipe; the cloud runs fal's InfiniteTalk without it. Say so in the model menu line / tagline on both engines and in Settings -> Models & licences ('your GPU adds the FusioniX LoRA; the cloud runs fal's InfiniteTalk without it'). Check fal (and Replicate) for an InfiniteTalk endpoint that takes LoRAs; if one exists, send FusioniX there through Fuobe's LoRA mirror, priced before running.

Add a blind A/B case to the evaluation harness (scripts/eval): Fuobe DoP vs Kling 2.5 Turbo on a representative set of the 32 effects, marked as the first suite to run when paid keys exist, with the rule written in scripts/eval/README.md and docs/STATUS.md: if Fuobe DoP clearly loses, the default goes back to Kling 2.5 Turbo (a reviewed code change).

archive-restore.title: Restore & colourise archive footage: LTX Restore IC-LoRA (+ Detail Refine) as a finishing ladder across the video tools
archive-restore.brief:
The owner asked for https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Restore (revision 79245e197a6cd3251e77d178dc380b0e9f2d6563; model card copy at @EXT@/ltx-restore/README.md, read as data). An IC-LoRA (1.7 GB, rank 128, LTX-2.x Community License; the repo is GATED on Hugging Face: downloads need an HF token after accepting its terms) trained on LTX-2.3 22B and tested on LTX-2.5 distilled: it takes archive video (low-res web rips, low-bitrate broadcast, tape, sepia or black-and-white scans) as a frame-aligned reference and renders the same shot clean, in colour, at high resolution. Recipe from the card: lanczos the clip to the working canvas (1440 wide for 4:3: 1440x1088; 1920x1088 for 16:9; multiples of 32; never stretch 4:3), tiled latent fusion with 960x544 tiles at 50% overlap (tiled at every size), LoRA strength 1.0 (a switch: 0.7 = off, 1.4 = over-tint), 8 distilled steps (sigmas 1.0, 0.99375, 0.9875, 0.98125, 0.975, 0.909375, 0.725, 0.421875, 0.0; euler), guidance 1.0, 8n+1 frames per pass (49 or 97), clips past 97 frames in 97-frame windows chained by the previous window's last 17 restored frames (LTXVAddGuide at frame 0); optional reference image at frame_idx -1 (native crops of faces, signs, true colours on a grey canvas, a second LTXAddVideoICLoRAGuide); deinterlace first (fieldmatch,yadif,decimate) for interlaced sources; prompt = period, place, light, materials, clothing, "natural colour"; negative = modern objects it must not invent. Stage 2 (optional, to 4K class): lanczos x2 and the Detail Refine IC-LoRA (Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Refine-Details, tile 1024x576) — restore first, refine second. ComfyUI: ComfyUI-LTXVideo's example LTX-2.5_V2V_TiledFusion_Upscale.json (Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo) with the LoRA swapped.

Fuobe already has LTX-2.5 open graphs and LTX-2.3 LoRA graphs (Fuobe DoP · LTX), the LTX-2.3 IC-LoRA Relight in the LoRA library, the Upscale / FPS Boost / SDR→HDR / Export finishing tools (r4/video-finish, Faceless upscale), SeedVR2 / ESRGAN chunked upscalers, and a LoRA mirror that fetches files before a run (src/server/loras.ts).
Build, as one "Restore & colourise" finishing feature:
1. Research record + LoRA library: both IC-LoRAs (Restore, Refine Details) pinned with sizes, licence and the gated-download fact; the ComfyUI-LTXVideo pack pinned in scripts/comfy/install-comfyui.sh if the tiled fusion nodes need it (read its code as data; report what the CPU server lacks, never install); an HF token setting (Settings → Connections, masked like other keys) used only to download gated files, with a clear message when it is missing.
2. CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED (the owner's rule): a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does. fal hosts LTX-2.3 IC-LoRAs on fal-ai/ltx-2.3-22b/reference-video-to-video/lora: fetch its schema; if it takes the reference video and a LoRA URL, add the cloud route (no tiling there: say the cloud runs one untiled pass at the endpoint's sizes, and price it before running); the gated file reaches fal through Fuobe's LoRA mirror with the user's HF token.
3. Spec + build + validate against the live CPU ComfyUI.
4. A prompt helper: from a few frames, write the period / place / light / clothing sentence and a negative list of modern objects (Claude, Ollama or Fuobe's open vision route; editable; the offline writer gives a template).

w2s-w3.title: Skills W3: Assist saves and runs skills
w2s-w3.brief:
Context: Fuobe (branch claude/fuobe-parity-4; this plan was written against 7d7a765) is an open-source 1:1 alternative to Higgsfield (image, video and audio studios, Assist, MCP, CLI, Canvas, Library). This package comes from docs/research/work2skill-7.md (research on Work2Skill: keep its demo-to-skill idea and authoring rules, drop the screen recording; build skills from Fuobe's exact records, give them typed inputs, check them by running them before saving, and replay them without an LLM). All packages: typecheck, lint, the full vitest suite and the browser checks pass; demo mode works without keys; docs/cli.md is updated when the CLI changes (docs/STATUS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md are left to the docs pass before each PR); read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing route handlers (AGENTS.md) and follow the existing routes' pattern (RouteContext, await connection()); licences are information, not gates; a cloud route only where a model is actually hosted.

Builds on W1 (the recipe format in docs/research/work2skill-7.md §9 and W1's runner, checks and Run dialog) and W2 (the review screen).

**Goal.** A chat that finally worked becomes a skill, and next time Assist (Claude, Ollama or the offline planner) fills its inputs and shows one priced card instead of planning from scratch. MCP clients get the same tool for free.

**User story.** "The chat made the dub-and-caption flow I wanted. I click Save as skill. Next week I type '/dub-and-caption' with a new clip, or just 'do the dub thing for this', and approve one card."

**Save this chat as a skill (recording and parameter detection from a chat).**
- Entry: the Assist header, beside **Schedule** (`src/components/assist-view.tsx` about line 163; lucide `BookmarkPlus`, label hidden below `lg` like Schedule), shown when the chat has a gated call that ran; and the chat ⋯ menu (`src/components/assist/chat-menu.tsx`): "Save as skill…".
- `draftFromThread(threadId)`: read `assist_threads.messages_json` and pair each assistant `tool_use` with its `tool_result` by `tool_use_id`. Keep calls to gated tools (`generate`, `create_storyboard`, `katana`, the studio tools in STUDIO_ROUTES) whose result isn't `is_error` and names started ids. This covers auto-run calls, which have no approval card in `items_json`. Drop declined calls (is_error "The user declined…"), errors and calls whose generations all failed. When the same tool was called again for the same output kind with changes, keep the last (a heuristic).
- `after` inside one `generate` call already makes chains. Across calls, an input that equals an output URL of an earlier kept call is a step reference: generate → generate merges into one pipeline, mapping the field to a chain slot (`images` → images, `end_image` → endImage, `video` → video, `audio` → audio, `voice_audio` → voiceAudio, `background_audio` → audio2). A cross-call reference into or out of a studio tool is refused in this package ("Skills can't wait for a studio step yet", W7). `create_storyboard` stays one tool step. The user's attachments become media candidates; the user's words go to the naming pass.
- Then W2's review screen.

**`run_skill` tool** (new `src/server/assist/skill-tools.ts`, pushed in `src/server/assist/tools.ts` beside `CONTEXT_TOOLS` and `STUDIO_TOOLS`, line 543): input `{ name, values?, rows? (≤ 50), engine? }`; gated; `plan` = `estimateRecipe` (atomic for a pipeline); `title` = the skill's title; `place` = the studio for a tool step; `run` = `runRecipe`. Bad values come back as an error listing the inputs ("needs product (image) and name (text)"). Because it's gated and in `TOOLS`, MCP lists it and `estimate_job` prices it (`jobTools()` in `src/server/mcp.ts`) with no MCP change beyond bumping `SERVER_INFO.version` to 1.3.0 and one sentence in its instructions.
- Context: the skill index (`src/server/assist/context.ts`, SKILL_INDEX 60) marks recipe skills "(runs by itself: run_skill with product, name)". Assist's system prompt: when a saved skill with a recipe fits, call `run_skill` with values from the message and attachments instead of re-planning.
- Offline planner (`offline` in `src/server/assist/agent.ts`, which already receives the chat's loaded skills): when a loaded skill (`/name` or a project skill) has a recipe, fill its media inputs from the message's attachments by kind and order, its first text input from the words, the rest from defaults or examples, and emit `run_skill`; if a required input is missing, reply naming it. No LLM.

**Storage.** None.

**Tests.** `tests/assist-skill-tools.test.ts`: `draftFromThread` on a stored thread with an approved `generate` chain, a declined call, an auto-run call (no card) and a failed call; a cross-call merge; a cross-call studio reference refused; `run_skill` plan and run in demo mode; the offline planner turns "/lamp-turntable" plus an attachment into a `run_skill` card. `tests/mcp.test.ts`: `tools/list` has `run_skill`, `estimate_job`'s enum includes it, version 1.3.0. Browser (extend `tests/e2e/assist-flows.mjs`): save a chat as a skill, then `/skill` plus an attachment in a new chat → approval card → run; 1440 and 390 px, light and dark.

**Demo mode.** All of it works on the offline planner and the mock provider. Live Claude and Ollama behaviour stays unverified (docs/STATUS.md, the 'Assist on Claude' and 'Assist on a local model' rows), and small local models follow tool instructions less reliably.

w2s-w4.title: Skills W4: Skills on a schedule and in the CLI
w2s-w4.brief:
Context: Fuobe (branch claude/fuobe-parity-4; this plan was written against 7d7a765) is an open-source 1:1 alternative to Higgsfield (image, video and audio studios, Assist, MCP, CLI, Canvas, Library). All packages: typecheck, lint, the full vitest suite and the browser checks pass; demo mode works without keys; docs/cli.md is updated when the CLI changes (docs/STATUS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md are left to the docs pass before each PR); read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing route handlers (AGENTS.md) and follow the existing routes' pattern (RouteContext, await connection()); licences are information, not gates; a cloud route only where a model is actually hosted.

Builds on W1 (the recipe format in docs/research/work2skill-7.md §9 and W1's runner, checks and Run dialog) and W3 (`run_skill`).

**Goal.** Run a fixed procedure on a timer or from a terminal, deterministically, with the same prices and caps.

**User story.** "Every Monday my 'weekly promo' skill runs on my newest upload with no LLM in the loop. A teammate runs it from the CLI with a CSV of 20 products."

**Schedules.**

Each media input can be a fixed file or **Newest upload of this kind (when it runs)**, read at run time from the newest upload asset of that kind.
- A skill run is a chat like today, so ask-first cards, the auto-run cap (default $2, DEFAULT_SCHEDULE_CAP_USD), `last_thread_id` and summaries keep working. `startSchedule` (`src/server/assist/schedules.ts`) already takes a `model` override: pass a fixed `ModelCall` that returns one `run_skill` `tool_use` with the task's values, then an `end_turn` reply. No LLM is called.
- Deleting or renaming a skill pauses its tasks with the reason, as a deleted project does (extend `renameSkillRefs` in `src/server/skills.ts`).

**Storage.** One migration, the next entry in `MIGRATIONS` (`src/server/db.ts`; it was index 23 at `7d7a765`, but ids are positional and other packages append migrations too: take the next free entry and let the migration tests decide): `ALTER TABLE assist_schedules ADD COLUMN skill_json TEXT` holding `{ name, values, sources }`. Add `skill_json` to the `assist_schedules` entry of `ASSET_REFS` in `src/server/generations.ts` (values hold file URLs) and document the migration in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**CLI** (`bin/lib/commands.mjs`, `bin/lib/skills.mjs`, `docs/cli.md`).
- `fuobe skills params <name>`: the inputs as text.
- `fuobe skills estimate <name> -p key=value… [--rows rows.csv] [--engine open|cloud]`.

[y/N]" unless `--yes` or `--json`; `--wait` and `--out` reuse generate's wait and download path.
- `fuobe skills export <name> [--examples] [--out file.zip]`: W1's zip.

**MCP.** Nothing beyond W3.

n7-7-exact-orbits.title: N7 7: Exact orbits in DoP, Cinema moves, Image to 3D and Canvas

It is a camera-path feature like N7-5's merged Fly path: on the open engine it is Uni3C (wan21-i2v-uni3c-path), and in the cloud it is hosted H3 Max camera-controls (with views: minimax-h3-max ref2v or FLUX 3 Max keyframes), as N7-5 and N7-6 already do. - Cinema's Director: the orbit moves (drone-orbit L363, arc-left L370, arc-right L372, bullet-time L367 in `src/lib/catalog/cinema.ts`; `CINEMA_CAMERA_LORA` is null for them, L606-615): the same switch in the move picker (`src/components/cinema/camera-moves.tsx`).

- Canvas (`src/lib/catalog/canvas.ts` `NODE_SPECS` L221): a "Camera path" node (preset or keys) and a "Fly around" node (image + optional views + path -> video).

Open engine.

- Image to 3D: record the finished GLB (Pixal3D or TRELLIS.2, after the server's GLB finish) or the TripoSplat result along the path as the render instead of a point cloud.
- Canvas and Assist run without a browser view, so they need a server-side render. Option A: pin Camera H3 Bruxos (NyckM/3d-Camera-control-H3-Minimax @ 36c4218a2561328436d440fa9134631ee515471b, Apache-2.0, no Python dependencies) and use `BruxosH3Camera` Depth Warp from core `MoGeInference`; its output is Meridian-shaped (73 / 90 / 107 / 124 ... frames at 24 fps, grey-128 holes), so resample to 81 frames at 16 fps and turn grey holes black. Option B: a small headless point-cloud renderer in Fuobe's server. Option A can't be /prompt-validated here: the shared server lacks the Bruxos pack and agents never install packs. Build option B (no new pack), and record option A in the report as an alternative the owner can try after installing the pinned pack.
- The ostris Wan 2.2 orbit LoRAs stay as the "Loose" choice.

Cloud engine. H3 Max camera-controls (N7-5) with the preset as keyframes; with reference views (Canvas "Fly around" with views), `minimax-h3-max` ref2v or FLUX 3 Max keyframes as in N7-6. 5 s at 768P = $0.40 at list price.

Browser checks: at 1440 px and 390 px wide, in light and in dark theme: the new controls render, labels and prices fit, nothing scrolls sideways, keyboard focus reaches every new control, and touch dragging works at 390 px. Here: the Exact switch and its controls on the Motions page and in Cinema's move picker; "Film it photoreal" in Image to 3D; the two Canvas nodes.

What can't be verified here: GPU runs and paid calls; whether the Bruxos pack loads on Fuobe's pin.

n7-9-worldcast-worker.title: N7 9: WorldCast on your GPU: the Fuobe Fly-Around Original's open half
n7-9-worldcast-worker.brief:
CLOUD, under the owner's rule (they chose GPU-only for DBS rather than a different hosted model): features built on Open-H3-Regenerate-2K and on WorldCast are GPU-only, because nobody hosts those models; do NOT route them to fal's H3 Max camera-controls, FLUX 3 Max keyframes or H3 2K-at-generation as stand-ins. Two things are fine: MOSS-Image is hosted on fal (fal-ai/moss-image, /lora), so it gets a cloud route; and where a feature already runs on fal's MiniMax H3 (Genjutsu / Character Swap Studio cloud swaps), asking that same hosted model for a higher resolution it offers is the same model, not a stand-in. SHARED PIECES: if the base already contains a camera-path editor / fly path (n7-5), a finishing ladder in Upscale (archive-restore or n7-3), or turnaround stills (qma-angles), reuse and extend them instead of building a second one.

Goal. Put the real WorldCast behind the Fly path (N7-5), Turnaround / Fly around (N7-6) and Exact orbit (N7-7) buttons on the open engine, so the back and sides follow the user's own reference views. WorldCast has no ComfyUI port and needs custom DiT code, so the first step is a worker; a Fuobe node pack can follow if the quality is worth it. Research: new-models-7.md §3.1-§3.6, §3.8, §3.11.

The worker (§3.6 option 1).
- Contract in `docs/workers/worldcast.md`, written like `docs/workers/tribe-v2.md`: an HTTP service on the user's GPU, outside ComfyUI. `POST /cases` (multipart: first_frame.png, person_mask.png, render.mp4, render_mask.mp4, cam_info.json with 81 camera-to-world poses in OpenCV convention and a 3x3 pixel intrinsic, up to four anchors {side, image, mask, azimuth}, an optional anchors_aligned_camera_info.json, prompt, seed, steps 50, cfg 5.0, shift 2.0, height 832, width 480) -> a job id; `GET /jobs/{id}` -> status and progress; `GET /jobs/{id}/video` -> the MP4 (81 frames at 15 fps). A setting `WORLDCAST_URL` (Settings -> Open-source engine, beside the isolated worker URL).
- A thin reference server in `workers/worldcast/` that imports PixCtrol/WorldCast @ 7ccf2e0ded1238bf6dea1b285c29bcf322e337cb (Apache-2.0) in its own virtualenv (the README's verified combination: torch 2.8.0+cu128 with transformers 5.8.1). Read WorldCast's code as data, at the pinned commit; never install or run it here. Weights: ly56/worldcast @ 27635f27a2f9414dd8b78542eb390b565a288a53 (`checkpoints/base_dit.safetensors` 8,401,611,192 B and `checkpoints/worldcast_bank.safetensors` 1,982,937,976 B; both from the same release) and Wan-AI/Wan2.1-I2V-14B-720P @ 8823af45fcc58a8aa999a54b04be9abc7d2aac98 (82.22 GB). The worker's README tells the user to check it first on `demo_case_traj5.json` on their own GPU; test Fuobe's client against a mock server only.

Fuobe prepares the case. Default depth: MoGe 2 or DA3 metric-large, chosen because they are already pinned and small. Also offer the paper's own Depth Pro and VGGT-Omega as options, each with its licence recorded as data (Apple research-only; FAIR-NC, a gated download that needs the HF token) and its switch in Settings -> Models & licences, like every other model.
- Depth: MoGe 2 (MIT, the 3D scene's `oss-scene-moge`) or Depth Anything 3 metric-large (Apache-2.0, Comfy-Org/Depth-Anything-3 @ 8265be07).
- Masks: core `SAM3_Detect` with the pinned `sam3.1_multiplex_fp16`.
- Path: `framePoses` from N7-5's library; `render.mp4` / `render_mask.mp4` from N7-5's recorder (mask 0 = covered, 255 = hole).
- Anchors: the element's or sheet's views with azimuths in WorldCast's convention (front 0°, right_side about 90°, back about 180°, left_side about 270°, `left_sign` -1); anchor poses on a ring at the subject distance (a guess), or leave `anchors_aligned_camera_info.json` out (the code then skips anchor Plücker rays; quality impact unknown).
- The `no_padding_black/` crops are not documented: read them from `demo_case/` and `diffsynth/pipelines/worldcast_pipeline.py` L842-869 before building.

Fuobe side.
- An open ModelDef `oss-worldcast` routed to the worker. The three buttons prefer it when `WORLDCAST_URL` answers, and otherwise fall back to the Uni3C graph / Frames chain with a line saying so ("Runs on Uni3C: add a WorldCast worker (48 GB+) for sides that match your photos").
- Output is portrait 480 x 832 at 15 fps; offer RIFE to 24 fps and the existing upscalers after it.

Licences as information (§3.5): WorldCast weights Apache-2.0 with the note that Stage 1 trained on SpatialVID (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) "strictly for academic research purposes" by the authors' statement; Wan 2.1 720P Apache-2.0; MoGe 2 MIT; DA3 Apache-2.0; SAM 3.1 SAM License. VGGT-Omega (FAIR-NC, gated) and Depth Pro (Apple research-only) recorded the same way, with the admin's switch.

Tests: the case builder (files, shapes, matrix conventions, the side -> azimuth map); the worker client against a mock server (submit, poll, download, errors); the fallback line when no worker answers; the ModelDef's visibility.

Browser checks: at 1440 px and 390 px wide, in light and in dark theme: the new controls render, labels and prices fit, nothing scrolls sideways, keyboard focus reaches every new control, and touch dragging works at 390 px. hi3d-refine.title: Hi3D 1.0 (formerly Sparc3D): high-resolution geometry refinement in Image to 3D, a print-ready export, and texture back on the refined mesh

The owner shared https://www.hi3d.ai/hi3d-1-0-open-source. Facts gathered (verify them; README and LICENSE copies are in @EXT@/hi3d/, read as data; never run or install their code here): Hi3D v1.0 is Sparc3D's second stage released open: it REFINES a coarse mesh into high-resolution geometry, conditioned on a reference image of the same object (it does not make a mesh from nothing: the README's example uses Hunyuan3D-2 for the coarse mesh). Output is geometry only (no textures, materials or vertex colours), recentred and normalised to unit radius, batch size one; resolutions 512, 1024 or 1536 (sparse extraction grid), 25 scheduler steps per pass. Code: github.com/hi3d-official/Hi3Dv1.0. 2. The open route: coarse mesh (from Pixal3D, TRELLIS.2 or Hunyuan3D 2.1, whichever the user picked) + the reference image -> Hi3D refine at 512 / 1024 / 1536 -> the refined mesh. Texture is not on the base: Fuobe has no Hunyuan3D-Paint graph, and TRELLIS.2's graph textures only its own shape. Ship the refined mesh as geometry only, labelled so. So Hi3D is open-engine only; the cloud engine says it runs on your GPU, and Engine mode 'Paid APIs only' hides it.
4. Placements: Image to 3D gains 'Refine detail · Hi3D 1.0' (a toggle and a resolution choice) on the open engine, also offered on any finished 3D result ('Refine this mesh'); a 'Print-ready' export (STL / 3MF of the refined geometry, with a watertight check and the unit-scale note, because Hi3D normalises the size: let the user set the real height); the Canvas 3D node offers the refine step; Assist / MCP. Show 'Powered by Hi3D 1.0' wherever its output is shown, as its licence asks.

idol-1.title: Idol 1: Idol 3D in Image to 3D -> Splat (open engine, core TripoSplat nodes, Best / Quick look, photo crop)
idol-1.brief:
GOAL. Add Speridlabs' Idol as a second open-engine model in Image to 3D -> Splat, named 'Idol 3D'. It runs on Fuobe's existing core TripoSplat graph with Idol's two weight files and Idol's reference sampler settings. Read docs/research/idol-9.md §2 (in and out; §2.3 same architecture as TripoSplat; §2.4 the haze), §3 (the claims: never promise seconds), §4 (weights and licences), §5.4-5.5 (the graph), §7, §8 and §9 idol-1.

WEIGHTS. In scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs KNOWN_MODELS, after the TripoSplat rows (L273-275), add two rows pinned to nynxz/Idol @ c718f2b1b95b353edd07d17e845719fc10880a44:
- 'idol_fp16.safetensors': { folder: 'diffusion_models', url: 'https://huggingface.co/nynxz/Idol/resolve/c718f2b1b95b353edd07d17e845719fc10880a44/diffusion_models/idol_fp16.safetensors' } (741,107,210 B, sha256 cf452146f78e23a0d34be8f9f79bcde642b9a40ef493046c8e9d5f79096f6dd0)
- 'idol_decoder_fp16.safetensors': { folder: 'vae', url: 'https://huggingface.co/nynxz/Idol/resolve/c718f2b1b95b353edd07d17e845719fc10880a44/vae/idol_decoder_fp16.safetensors' } (576,148,658 B, sha256 c511d99eb668ec4b06d883cb6e43770bc35e3864e16e7058e8d6211ba5c509aa)
Add a comment saying these are a third-party conversion (ComfyUI-Idol scripts/convert.py at 4d3a4f6) of speridlabs/idol @ 2731c229 (Apache-2.0): pos_pe dropped (ComfyUI recomputes it), cast to fp16, the two decoders merged under octree./gs., and spot-checked as faithful on 10 tensor prefixes (§3, §4.1). dino_v3_vit_h (L273), flux2-vae (L230) and birefnet (L168) are already listed and shared with TripoSplat, so only 1.32 GB is new. Optional in the same package: move 'flux2-vae.safetensors' from Comfy-Org/flux2-dev to the renamed Comfy-Org/Flux-2-Dev (the old URL is a 307 redirect; same sha256 d64f3a68...), rebuild, and check that only URL strings change in workflows/comfyui/manifest.json.

GRAPH. New scripts/comfy/hand-built/image-to-splat-idol.json: a copy of hand-built/image-to-splat-triposplat.json with the same node ids and these changes (§5.5):
- 88:16 UNETLoader unet_name 'idol_fp16.safetensors' (weight_dtype default).
- 88:11 VAELoader vae_name 'idol_decoder_fp16.safetensors'.
- 88:6 KSampler steps 50, cfg 4.0, sampler_name 'euler', scheduler 'simple', denoise 1. Idol's CFG weight 3, in its (1+w)cond - w*uncond form, is ComfyUI cfg 4. Its rescale_t 3 is TripoSplat's built-in shift 3 (comfy/supported_models.py L1677-1679), so no ModelSamplingSD3 node is needed.
- Photo crop branch (core nodes; my analysis): 88:101 ImageScale {image [88:2,0], upscale_method 'lanczos', width 720, height 720, crop 'disabled'}; 88:102 EmptyImage {width 1024, height 1024, batch_size 1, color 0}; 88:103 ImageCompositeMasked {destination [88:102,0], source [88:101,0], x 152, y 152, resize_source false}; 88:104 ComfySwitchNode {switch false, on_false [88:2,0], on_true [88:103,0]}; 88:24 TripoSplatConditioning image [88:104,0] (was [88:2,0]). TripoSplatPreprocessImage (88:2) is Idol's 'synthetic' 1.2 crop. Scaled to 720 and centred on a black 1024 canvas, the object spans 600 px; Idol's 'real' 1.7 crop gives 602 px. ComfySwitchNode inputs are lazy (comfy_extras/nodes_logic.py L98-111), so the branch not taken does not run.
- 75 RenderSplat opacity_threshold 0.05 (was 0): the orbit video drops the near-transparent haze (§2.4). The saved file still has it; idol-2 prunes it.
- 88:96 (a ComfySwitchNode whose two inputs are the same UNETLoader) can stay as it is.
- Everything else stays as in the TripoSplat file: 99 LoadImage, the cut-out switch 88:35 (BiRefNet 88:85:81/82 or the PNG's own alpha via 88:95), 88:7 CLIPVisionLoader dino_v3_vit_h, 88:8 VAELoader flux2-vae, 88:55 VAEDecodeTripoSplat, 92 SplatToFile3D (spz), 51 SaveGLB 'fuobe/splat', 79 CreateCameraInfo orbit 35/30/2.5, 41 CreateVideo 25 fps h264, 42 SaveVideo 'fuobe/splat-orbit'.

SPEC ENTRY. In scripts/comfy/library.spec.mjs, right after image-to-splat-triposplat (L3349-3372), add:
- id 'image-to-splat-idol', title 'Image to a Gaussian splat of one object (Idol on the TripoSplat core nodes) + an orbit video', capability 'splat', handBuilt 'hand-built/image-to-splat-idol.json'.
- bindings: TripoSplat's (image 99.image; cutout 88:35.switch; numGaussians 88:55.num_gaussians; steps and cfg 88:6; seed 88:6.seed and 88:55.seed; splatFormat 92.format; orbitFrames 75.frames; filenamePrefix 51 and 42), plus sampler: [b('88:6','sampler_name')] and photoCrop: [b('88:104','switch')].
- outputs [{node '51', kind 'model3d', role 'splat'}, {node '42', kind 'video', role 'turntable'}]; defaults { splatFormat: 'spz', cutout: true, photoCrop: false }; limits { maxGaussians: 1048576 }; vramGb 8.
- license: 'Apache-2.0 (speridlabs/idol weights; the ComfyUI files are nynxz/Idol's conversion, Apache-2.0); Idol is VAST-AI-Research's TripoSplat architecture (MIT, code and weights); the dino_v3_vit_h image encoder is under the DINOv3 License (royalty-free, commercial use allowed, trade-control limits; the app must show a "Built with DINOv3" notice); FLUX.2 VAE Apache-2.0; BiRefNet MIT'. Keep the DINOv3 wording identical to TripoSplat's so licenceInfo (src/lib/licences.ts L296ff) finds the notice.
- notes: the reference settings and where they come from, the Quick preset, the photo crop and how it was derived, 'about half the Gaussians are near-transparent: RenderSplat thresholds 0.05; the saved file is not pruned without the ComfyUI-Idol pack', 1.32 GB of new weights (idol_fp16 0.74, idol_decoder_fp16 0.58) plus the shared 2.46 GB, and 'VRAM: vendor peak 7.2 GB in the SDK; unmeasured in ComfyUI. Names, orders and line numbers in this brief predate it. Since then (fd09201, b5ca728): accounts can't start any 3D model yet (POST /api/generations answers 403 own-gpu-tool, and createGenerations refuses it too). MAIN CHANGED THIS AREA (10-30): main's GPU pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS and the preset map in src/server/gpu/tools.ts; chips from /api/gpu/badges) shows every studio, app and model as Ready / One step away / Needs setup / Needs a bigger GPU. PUBLIC SIGN-UP (the owner's, on main: docs/public-signup.md at your base, which wins where it says more than this; the accounts lane acc-* was dropped on 2026-10-30, and docs/research/accounts-8.md is background research only): every route, tool, page and run you add follows it the way main's own routes do. Read src/lib/guest-access.ts, src/proxy.ts, src/server/tenant.ts and tests/public-signup.test.ts first. Guests browse read-only (changes answer 401). Accounts see the owner's library as a guest does: the owner's lists come back empty (EMPTY_LISTS), other reads of them are refused, a change to the library or projects goes in LIBRARY_CHANGES (403 code library), and a visitor is never told whether one of the owner's records exists. Install-wide settings, keys and tokens stay the owner's (OWNER_WRITES, OWNER_ALL). Only the owner's runs reach the install's keys: an account runs studio generations through POST /api/generations on its own GPU (a linked ComfyUI, its own computer through its tab, or a ComfyUI paired with Fuobe Connect, docs/gpu-workers.md; onOwnGpu in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts; accountRun in src/server/generations.ts keeps chained steps the account's own); without one any run answers connect-gpu, and a tool that plans with the studio's own AI helpers or keeps projects of its own answers own-gpu-tool (so does every 3D model for now). Hosted runs (FUOBE_HOSTED_RUNS=1, off by default; "Hosted runs" in docs/public-signup.md): an account's studio run through POST /api/generations may run on the install's own ComfyUI server instead (decidePlace in src/server/hosted-run.ts, src/server/hosted.ts), priced and set aside by an optional billing service and checked by an optional moderation service; a model or op you add on that path plans and prices there too (poolQuote; test it in the style of tests/hosted-runs.test.ts), while Image to 3D, extra LoRAs, and clips and sound as inputs stay on the account's own GPU, and every other tool still answers own-gpu-tool. An account's run reads only its own files: it runs inside runAsTenant, src/server/tenant.ts says what work inside a tenant may use, and src/server/account-inputs.ts checks every input (input-not-allowed, input-not-yours, input-gone, input-too-big). A new server path that reads, fetches or chains a file for a run goes through them, with a test in the style of tests/account-tenant.test.ts and the other tests/account-*.test.ts. A price check (an estimate route, or ?preview=1 on a run route) goes in ESTIMATES or PREVIEWS and runs through priceAs (src/server/visitor.ts), so a visitor is priced for its own GPU on the open engine, never a demo. The sign-in proxy holds a request body only up to 4 MB (main, 10-31: proxyClientMaxBodySize in next.config.ts; a bigger body reaches the route cut short, with no error), so a route that takes a large file takes an uploaded file's reference instead (POST /api/uploads skips the proxy through src/server/direct-gate.ts). - map params.extra.photoCrop true -> cropMode 'real' and false -> 'synthetic'.
