- The provider picks the clean graph when object_info lists IdolPruneSplat and the core graph when it does not.
- Bindings for cropMode / minOpacity / maxScale, and the photoCrop -> cropMode mapping.
- The licence row (NODE_PACKS) and the workflow licence.

idol-4.title: Idol 4: Look around splats in Fuobe: a three.js splat viewer on result cards, the studio panel and the Library
idol-4.brief:
GOAL. Let people look around a Gaussian splat inside Fuobe instead of watching a fixed orbit video or downloading it to SuperSplat. This helps Idol 3D and both TripoSplat routes. Read idol-9.md §2.1 (formats), §2.4 (the haze), §7.1 (viewers today) and §9 idol-4. Does not depend on idol-1.

WHERE.
- src/components/model3d/model-card.tsx: the splat note at L177 and the download row.
- src/components/studio/result-media.tsx: the splat panel at L248.
- The Library's 3D tab (src/components/library-view.tsx L58), using the same viewer component.
- The viewer that 'View in 3D' opens (src/lib/output-actions.ts L146).
Formats come from splatFormatOf (src/lib/av/model3d.ts L197): spz, ply, ksplat.

LIBRARY. A three.js Gaussian-splat renderer; three 0.183.2 is already a dependency (package.json L56). Candidates are Spark (@sparkjsdev/spark) and GaussianSplats3D (@mkkellogg/gaussian-splats-3d). The choice is a guess. Check:
- the licence;
- an exact version at least two weeks old;
- .spz support (Niantic, gzip) and .ply with degree-0 SH;
- WebGL2;
- phone frame time on a 262,144-Gaussian splat;
- bundle size.
Load it with a dynamic import so no other page pays for it. Record the decision and the numbers in idol-9.md.

UI. A SplatViewer component with:
- drag to orbit, pinch / wheel to zoom, and reset view;
- a light / dark / grey background;
- an opacity cut-off slider labelled 'Hide faint haze' (default 0.05 for Idol 3D results; 0 for TripoSplat until idol-3 says otherwise);
- 'Save a still' (canvas capture -> upload -> Library image, like Cinema's capture);
- keyboard access and labels.
The orbit video stays as the poster while loading, and as the fallback when there is no WebGL2, when prefers-reduced-motion is set, or for files over a size limit. Replace 'Fuobe doesn't draw splats yet' with the viewer, and keep the download buttons.

TESTS.
- Unit: format detection and the choice between the splat viewer and the GLB viewer; the cut-off default per model; a parser test on a tiny .ply fixture if the library exposes one.
- e2e: open a demo splat at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark; no horizontal scroll; the viewer does not load on pages without a splat (bundle check).

idol-3.brief:
GOAL. Use measured numbers, not the vendor's table, to decide three things: which open splat model is Splat mode's default (TripoSplat today or Idol 3D), what Idol's Quick preset should be, and whether the photo crop helps photos. Read idol-9.md §3 (the vendor-only quality claim), §7.2 and §9 idol-3, and scripts/eval/README.md (the promote rule: a person changes a default in a reviewed commit). Builds on idol-1, and on idol-2 if it is merged.

SUITE. scripts/eval/cases/splat.json, validated by case.schema.json:
- suite 'splat', title 'Splat · one object from one picture', kind 'video'. The orbit video is the main output: scripts/eval/lib/review.mjs L19 and covers.mjs L66 pick the first image or video that is not a mask, so the turntable is scored and shown. The .spz is kept as a file.
- targets: open { models: ['oss-idol', 'oss-triposplat'] }, and demo.
Variants:
- 'idol-best': oss-idol, extra { steps 50, sampler 'euler', cfg 4, numGaussians 262144 }
- 'idol-quick': oss-idol, extra { steps 20, sampler 'dpmpp_2m', cfg 4, numGaussians 65536 }
- 'triposplat-today': oss-triposplat with its manifest defaults (20 dpmpp_2m, cfg 3)
- 'triposplat-50': oss-triposplat at 50 euler, cfg 4. This separates the weights from the settings. It needs 'sampler' bound in TripoSplat's entry too; otherwise skip this variant.
- 'idol-photo-crop', on the photo cases: idol-best with photoCrop true (and cropMode 'real' when idol-2 is merged)
Cases: 8-12 single objects, with inputs under local/splat/ (never committed) and demoInputs from fixtures/. Include generated product renders (bottle, sneaker, headphones), product photos (photo crop on), a figurine, a stylised character, a realistic person, thin parts (chair, plant), and glass or chrome. references = the input picture.
Metrics:
- 'style' with --style-model dinov2 (orbit frames against the input picture; DINOv2 is Apache-2.0), 'temporal' (orbit smoothness) and 'aesthetic'.
- The harness's timing and memory telemetry.
- The blind A/B review page (pnpm eval:review) for the turntables.
- Optional, only if cheap: a 'splat' metric that reads the .ply / .spz and reports the share of Gaussians under opacity 0.05. It would answer whether TripoSplat has Idol's haze.

OUTPUT. There is no GPU here: add a 'Results (pending a GPU run)' section to idol-9.md with the exact commands to run (the harness's run for these cases on the open engine; scripts/eval/README.md) and what each number decides. Never record demo-engine numbers as results, and leave §3 and §7.2 unchanged until a GPU run. The default change itself (MODELS_3D.splat.open order in src/lib/av/model3d.ts, IDOL_PRESETS) goes in a separate commit that a person reviews and makes after that run.

TESTS. pnpm eval:validate (schema), a demo dry run (pnpm eval:run --suite splat --engine demo --dry-run) and a demo run. Any new metric gets pytest fixtures like the others (scripts/eval/metrics).

MUST NOT BREAK. Other suites, the case schema's existing kinds (image, video, audio), and the promote rule.

VERIFY HERE. Schema and demo runs only. GPU runs need a machine with an 8-16 GB GPU and the weights. Record the GPU, driver and ComfyUI version with the numbers.

idol-7.title: Idol 7: Idol 3D quick mesh: splat -> core SplatToMesh -> .glb in From an image
idol-7.brief:
GOAL. A rough, riggable mesh from one picture: core ComfyUI turns Idol's splat into a vertex-coloured .glb. Read idol-9.md §2.1 (no mesh), §2.4 (min_opacity), §8 and §9 idol-7. Builds on idol-1.

GRAPH. scripts/comfy/hand-built/image-to-mesh-idol.json:
- idol-1's graph, then core SplatToMesh ('Extract Mesh from Splat', comfy_extras/nodes_gaussian_splat.py L1533-1580). Its defaults are resolution 384 and min_opacity 0.02, which drops the haze.
- then SaveGLB 'fuobe/idol-mesh' (output role mesh). Keep the orbit video.
- bindings: idol-1's, plus 'meshResolution' (SplatToMesh.resolution) if exposed.
- spec entry: capability 'image-to-3d', vramGb 8, the same licence string.

MODEL AND UI.
- ModelDef 'oss-idol-mesh', name 'Idol 3D quick mesh', kind 'model3d', route comfy('image-to-3d', 'image-to-mesh-idol'), tagline 'A rough vertex-coloured .glb from one picture, no textures · 8 GB GPU · Apache-2.0 · Built with DINOv3'.
- Add it to MODELS_3D.image.open after oss-hunyuan3d-21, with the note 'Rough mesh, vertex colours, no textures · 8 GB GPU'.
- The .glb opens in model-viewer and can go to Rig & animate (cloud Meshy rigging, as for any GLB today).

EVAL FIRST. Mesh quality from Idol splats is unknown (§11). Add 3-4 cases to idol-3's suite (or a 'mesh' variant) and look at the meshes before shipping.

LATER. hi3d-refine (earlier in this lane) offers 'Refine this mesh' on finished 3D results. Check that it shows on oss-idol-mesh results with the source picture (model3dView.photo) as its reference, or hide it there with a reason. Don't build a second Hi3D path.

TESTS. The spec entry, bindings, the route, MODELS_3D order, collectOutputs (the GLB comes back as model3d, not as a splat), and the licence row.

MUST NOT BREAK. oss-trellis2 and oss-hunyuan3d-21 stay first in From an image; the splat routes keep working.

idol-8.title: Idol 8: Fill the other sides from one picture (IdolCamera + RenderSplat, four views)
idol-8.brief:
GOAL. Side and back views of an object from one picture, consistent with each other, for the places that need several angles. Read idol-9.md §5.1 (IdolCamera), §8 and §9 idol-8. Needs idol-2's pack (IdolCamera) and idol-1.

GRAPH. scripts/comfy/hand-built/image-to-views-idol.json, with packs ['ComfyUI-Idol']:
- the clean Idol graph -> IdolCamera {samples [88:6,0]} -> RenderSplat {splat (pruned), camera_info from IdolCamera, frames 4, width / height 1024, opacity_threshold 0.05, background white or the studio's grey} -> SaveImage (one batch of four).
- RenderSplat with frames > 1 orbits a full turn from camera_info, 360/n degrees apart (comfy_extras/nodes_gaussian_splat.py L1004-1006). A negative frames value turns the other way.
- outputs: four images with meta.index 0-3; front (index 0) is the input view.
- match the orbit direction to Fuobe's side names (front, left, back, right; SIDES_HINT in src/lib/av/model3d.ts L80-88: 'facing its front, walk round to your right for its left side'). Pick the sign of frames so that index 1 is the object's left, and test it with an asymmetric object.

PLACES. Both are open engine only. Say in the UI that the views are renders of a 3D guess and may be soft.
- Image to 3D -> From several images: with only the front filled, a button 'Make the other sides from the front (Idol 3D)' runs the graph and fills the left, back and right slots for oss-trellis2-multi (VIEW_SIDES order).
- Elements (character and product references): 'Add side and back views'.

TESTS. The spec entry with packs, the bindings, the side mapping (index -> side), the multi-view slot filling, and the chain into oss-trellis2-multi.

MUST NOT BREAK. From several images when the user brings real photos, and Elements' existing uploads.

idol-9.brief:

o12-training-kit.title: O12: the training kit for Fuobe's own LoRAs and the motion library (specs, data-licence log, hosting), without training
o12-training-kit.brief:
The plan's "O12 · Train Fuobe's own LoRAs and the motion library" (docs/research/fuobe-originals-recipes-5.md) and §6 "LoRAs Fuobe should train itself". START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there. Nothing can be trained here (no GPU, no paid keys, no owned dataset), so this package builds everything up to the training run, honestly labelled as not yet run:
1. scripts/train/: one job spec per §6 LoRA (fuobe-soul-core, fuobe-cctv, fuobe-ultrawide-05 first, then the Wan 2.2 I2V LoRAs for Eyes In / Mouth In, Timelapse and Drone Reveal), each with both routes: an AI-Toolkit config for the user's GPU and the fal trainer payload (fal-ai/wan-22-trainer/i2v-a14b etc., from the research JSON), dataset size and caption rules, steps, rank, trigger, and the target library entry.
2. A data-licence log format (per LoRA: every image/clip source, its licence or ownership proof, consent where people appear) and a checker script that refuses to start a job whose dataset log is incomplete.
3. The LoRA library: a test that rejects any library entry without a licence snapshot; the planned own LoRAs appear as "planned" entries that no preset uses until a trained file exists.
4. The motion library: a manifest format for short CC0 or own-shot driving clips for the 13 sports moves (Wan Animate 2 / SCAIL-2), a checker for licence fields, and where those moves would pick the clips up once present (they keep their current route until then).
5. Hosting: how trained files are published to a Fuobe Hugging Face org (a script that uploads a file plus its data-licence log, dry-run by default) and how gen:catalog then picks them up.
6. A short guide in scripts/train/README.md. Tests for the specs, checkers and library rules.

w2s-w5.title: Skills W5: Skills as canvases
w2s-w5.brief:
Context: Fuobe (branch claude/fuobe-parity-4; this plan was written against 7d7a765) is an open-source 1:1 alternative to Higgsfield (image, video and audio studios, Assist, MCP, CLI, Canvas, Library). This package comes from docs/research/work2skill-7.md (research on Work2Skill: keep its demo-to-skill idea and authoring rules, drop the screen recording; build skills from Fuobe's exact records, give them typed inputs, check them by running them before saving, and replay them without an LLM). All packages: typecheck, lint, the full vitest suite and the browser checks pass; demo mode works without keys; docs/cli.md is updated when the CLI changes (docs/STATUS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md are left to the docs pass before each PR); read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing route handlers (AGENTS.md) and follow the existing routes' pattern (RouteContext, await connection()); licences are information, not gates; a cloud route only where a model is actually hosted.

Builds on W1 (the recipe format in docs/research/work2skill-7.md §9 and W1's runner, checks and Run dialog) and W2 (the review screen).

**Goal.** See and edit a skill's steps on the Canvas, and turn a canvas into a skill with a form, which makes canvases reachable from Assist, MCP, the CLI and schedules for the first time.

**User story.** "I open my skill as a canvas to swap a model visually, then save it back. Or I built a canvas and want my team to run it from a form."

**Converter** (pure, in `src/lib/catalog/canvas.ts`): `recipeToCanvas(recipe)` and `canvasToRecipe(graph, page)`. Inputs become input nodes (prompt/text, image, video, audio, element); steps become model nodes, with edges from chain slots. Canvas → recipe (the canvas is the 'demo'): unconnected input nodes become inputs (Fixed by default), model nodes become generate steps (their request as `describeNode` builds it), and concatenator and Table nodes compile the way `runCanvas` does (`concatRequest`, `rowRequest`); Table rows become the Many tab's rows (text inputs only, at most 50 × 8, `TABLE_LIMITS`). **Storage.** None (`canvases.graph_json`).

**Goal.** Notice repeated work and offer to save it (AWM-style online induction), and keep saved skills healthy as the catalog changes.

**User story.** "Fuobe notices I've made the same 'cut-out, scene, upscale' chain four times this week and offers to save it. My skill tells me when a step starts failing and suggests a fix."

A sweep (when the Library opens, at most once a day, server side in `src/server/recipes.ts`) groups the last 14 days of DAGs by shape. When one shape appears 3 or more times and no saved recipe has it, the Library shows a card above the grid in the All view (`src/components/library-view.tsx`, under the filters; full width at 390 px): "You've made 'cut-out → scene → turntable' 4 times. Save it as a skill?" with **Make a skill** (W2 with the newest run's rows), **Not now** and **Don't suggest this**. Dismissed shapes live in a settings row `skills.suggestions` (JSON; no migration). Under public sign-up that row is the owner's (accounts can't change settings): the sweep reads the owner's own generations (accounts' runs stay out of the owner's lists), and accounts get no suggestions.
- **Run history** per skill from generations whose `request_json` `$.skill.name` matches (`json_extract`; no new table): runs, success rate, spend, last run and favourites. Shown as a **History** section in the skill dialog (`src/components/assist/skills-view.tsx`, under Files): the last 10 runs with status, cost, date and a link to the run's batch in the Library.
- **Fix suggestions (verification upkeep).** A step that failed in 2 of the last 5 runs, was moved by `REPLACED_BY`, or was switched off in Models & licences gets **Suggest a fix** on the skill's "Needs a re-check" line: models with the same op and kind that are on (the `search_models` logic), with their prices. The user picks one; W1's plan and demo checks run; then it saves. Never swapped automatically.
- **Finding skills (Assist).** Past `SKILL_INDEX` (60, `src/server/assist/context.ts`), rank `list_skills` (`src/server/assist/context-tools.ts`, word match today) and the context index by word match, use count (from history) and recency, so the most used recipe skills are always in Assist's context.
- **Evaluation.** `pnpm eval:from-skill <name>` writes a `scripts/eval` case from the recipe's examples and checks, so the harness can regression-test a skill on a GPU or the cloud under its spend cap.
- **Storage.** None (a settings row and `request_json`).
- **Demo mode.** Suggestions and history work on demo rows; a suggestion built from demo rows says so.
- **Tests.** `tests/skill-suggest.test.ts`: the same chain with different prompts and inputs has one shape; helper and `eval` rows are ignored; the 3-in-14-days threshold; dismissal; no suggestion for a shape a saved recipe has. `tests/recipes.test.ts`: history from the `skill` stamp; fix candidates share op and kind and are switched on; ranking puts a used skill first. Browser: the suggestion card and the History section at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, in demo mode.

w2s-w7.title: Skills W7: Skills that span studios
w2s-w7.brief:
Context: Fuobe (branch claude/fuobe-parity-4; this plan was written against 7d7a765) is an open-source 1:1 alternative to Higgsfield (image, video and audio studios, Assist, MCP, CLI, Canvas, Library). Builds on W1 (the recipe format in docs/research/work2skill-7.md §9 and W1's runner, checks and Run dialog) and W3 (`run_skill`, `draftFromThread`).

**Goal.** Let a studio step feed later steps, and a generate step feed a studio step ("dub, then captions, then a 9:16 cut"), which needs waiting across modules that `createPipeline` can't validate as one (studio tools run through STUDIO_ROUTES, `src/server/assist/studio-tools.ts` / `studio-routes.ts`, and return a StudioRun).

**User story.** "My 'Spanish short' skill dubs the clip, burns captions and cuts a 9:16 version. I start it once and each step starts by itself."

- **Format.** Recipe version 2 (version 1 files still load): `{{steps.<key>.output}}` (the step's first output of the kind the field takes) in a tool step's input or a generate step's input, and tool steps anywhere in the order. `recipeProblems` checks that every reference points at an earlier step of a kind that fits.
- **Builder.** W3's `draftFromThread` stops refusing cross-call references into and out of studio tools and writes them as step references.
- **Runner.** `runRecipe` creates a `skill_runs` row, starts every step whose inputs exist (generate DAG parts through `createPipeline`, tool steps through `executeTool`, keeping each `StudioRun`'s ids and `href`), and a sweep (like the scheduled tasks' 30 s sweep, started with the generation runner) starts each waiting step when the generations it needs succeed. A failure fails the steps after it and says which step and why. `createPipeline`'s `existing` option may link later generate steps to a studio's result ids directly (a guess; untested).
- **Checks.** Plan check per step, with stand-in files for step references. Studio dry runs: a new `src/server/demo-scope.ts` (`runAsDemo(fn)` and `inDemoScope()` on `AsyncLocalStorage`; neither exists yet); `chooseRoute` returns the demo route inside the scope and rows created inside it get `request.demo` (W1's flag), so studio modules run as demos with no change to their code; the check then deletes the studio records it made (dub session, Layers project…).
- **Running** from every place W1, W3 and W4 added (Run dialog, `run_skill`, schedules, CLI): the result names the run and which steps wait; `run_skill`'s result says so to the agent.
- **UI.** The Run toast links to the run's progress, shown in the skill dialog (`src/components/assist/skills-view.tsx`; in W6's History section when W6 has shipped, else a Runs section of its own): "Dub · done → Captions · running → 9:16 cut · waiting", each with "Open in <Studio>" when the studio gave a page.
- **Storage.** One migration (the next `MIGRATIONS` entry in `src/server/db.ts`): `skill_runs` (id, skill, values_json, state_json with each step's status, generation ids and studio href, created_at, updated_at), with `values_json` and `state_json` in `ASSET_REFS`; documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **Demo mode.** The whole chain runs on the mock provider.
- **Tests.** `tests/skill-runs.test.ts`: a dub → captions → reframe recipe in demo mode starts the dub, waits, then starts the rest; a failed dub fails the rest with its reason; state survives a restart (reloaded from `skill_runs`); the studio dry run deletes its records. Browser: the run's progress in the skill dialog at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark.

nm10-kling-4.title: Kling 4.0 in the cloud: 3-30 s takes, multi-shot, references and video edit, now that fal's API is open
nm10-kling-4.brief:
WHY. Kling 4.0 is the flagship closed video model of the month (Higgsfield has offered it since 2026-10-21). Round 4 recorded its four fal endpoints but held them back as 'playground-only'. On 2026-11-01 the llms.txt pages for kling/v4/text-to-video and kling/v4/video-to-video/edit document live fal.run endpoints with no 'coming soon', and Replicate lists kwaivgi/kling-v4.0. It is the cheapest big win: catalog work only.
WHERE IT SHOWS UP. Video studio model menu (Best list), Cinema Studio takes (multi-shot up to 30 s, @Elements), Edit video (Kling 4 edit), Genjutsu Swap / Insert model picker, Assist and MCP model lists.
Research record: docs/research/paid-model-apis-4.json already holds kling/v4/text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video and video-to-video/edit with status 'playground-only' (catalog date 2026-10-16) and a recommendation not to route until the page drops "API access is coming soon". On 2026-11-01 https://fal.ai/models/kling/v4/text-to-video/llms.txt and .../video-to-video/edit/llms.txt describe live endpoints (fal.run, Key auth) with no waitlist (docs/research/new-models-10.md §2.2). FIRST re-fetch all four OpenAPI schemas with the existing scripts (the same way round 4 did) and confirm image-to-video and reference-to-video are live too; flip each record's status to active only if its page is live, and note the date. Replicate: replicate.com/explore lists kwaivgi/kling-v4.0 ("3-30 second videos up to 1080p and edits existing videos"): fetch its schema and add it as a second provider only if its inputs map cleanly.
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there.
Facts to build on (from the fal pages; re-check): text-to-video takes prompt OR multi_prompt (a list of shots whose durations sum to the total), duration 3-30 s (default 5), resolution 720p | 1080p (default 1080p), aspect_ratio 16:9 | 9:16 | 1:1 | 21:9; $0.157/s at 720p, $0.235/s at 1080p. image-to-video adds start_image_url (required) and end_image_url. reference-to-video takes image_urls, video_urls, elements, start_image_url, multi_prompt. video-to-video/edit takes prompt (the source is @Video1), video_url (3-30.05 s, <= 300 MB, 700-4553 px a side, aspect 0.40-2.50, 23.9-60.05 fps), image_urls (@Image1..), video_urls (up to 4, @Video2..; source + references + element videos <= 30 s in all), elements (up to 7; up to 3 with a voice_id, up to 3 video elements), voice_ids (up to 3, made with fal's create-voice model), duration 3-30, resolution; billed $0.094/s (720p) or $0.141/s (1080p) on input plus output seconds with a minimum of 2x the output. Kling's own spec (atlascloud summary of the release note) adds 10 keyframes, 15 mixed references, 10-bit HDR "coming soon" and 2-minute extension "coming soon": the fal API exposes none of the keyframe, HDR or extension features, so do not claim them.
Build:
1. scripts/gen-cloud-models.py: model("kling-4", "Kling 4.0", "Kuaishou", "kling", "video", ...) with routes t2v, i2v, flf2v (start + end image), ref2v (images, clips, @Elements) and v2v (edit), price per second by resolution, and the edit / clip-reference billing rule (input + output seconds, minimum 2x output) in the price function, never shown as the plain per-second rate. Regenerate src/lib/catalog/cloud-models.generated.ts (pnpm gen:catalog). Badges: top, 30s. Place it in the Video studio's Best list next to Seedance 2.5 and FLUX 3 Max.

nm10-h3-any-gpu.title: MiniMax H3 on 8-24 GB GPUs, and faster H3 decoding: FastH3 V2 and Trim tiers, Sol-H3-VAE and the core H3 latent upscaler
nm10-h3-any-gpu.brief:

nm10-pika-flex.title: Pika H3 Flex on your GPU: 6-step H3 with sound, and a References mode (up to 9 images, 3 clips and 3 voice or music clips) for the Video studio, Cinema and Lipsync
nm10-pika-flex.brief:
WHY. Pika open-sourced its post-trained MiniMax H3 on 2026-10-29 as two LoRA adapters with three official ComfyUI templates: 6 steps instead of 8-20, Pika's reward-tuned look, and a Ref2VA mode that takes ordered image, video and audio references in one call (reference-to-video, motion transfer, character swap, talking from a voice clip). Pika says it is #1 among open-weight models on DesignArena text-to-video. 2. oss-minimax-h3: a Quality choice 'Fast · Pika Flex (6 steps)' beside Standard (Turbo v4, 8) and Sharper (20). Since it needs the Ref2VA partition too, show the extra download on /connect.
3. CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED (the owner's rule): a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does.
MAIN CHANGED THIS AREA (10-30): main's GPU pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS and the preset map in src/server/gpu/tools.ts; chips from /api/gpu/badges) shows every studio, app and model as Ready / One step away / Needs setup / Needs a bigger GPU. Install-wide settings, keys and tokens stay the owner's (OWNER_WRITES, OWNER_ALL). Only the owner's runs reach the install's keys: an account runs studio generations through POST /api/generations on its own GPU (a linked ComfyUI, its own computer through its tab, or a ComfyUI paired with Fuobe Connect, docs/gpu-workers.md; onOwnGpu in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts; accountRun in src/server/generations.ts keeps chained steps the account's own); without one any run answers connect-gpu, and a tool that plans with the studio's own AI helpers or keeps projects of its own answers own-gpu-tool (so does every 3D model for now). A new server path that reads, fetches or chains a file for a run goes through them, with a test in the style of tests/account-tenant.test.ts and the other tests/account-*.test.ts. A price check (an estimate route, or ?preview=1 on a run route) goes in ESTIMATES or PREVIEWS and runs through priceAs (src/server/visitor.ts), so a visitor is priced for its own GPU on the open engine, never a demo. The sign-in proxy holds a request body only up to 4 MB (main, 10-31: proxyClientMaxBodySize in next.config.ts; a bigger body reaches the route cut short, with no error), so a route that takes a large file takes an uploaded file's reference instead (POST /api/uploads skips the proxy through src/server/direct-gate.ts). nm10-qwen21-fast.brief:

Together they make 2.1 several times faster and usable on 16 GB cards. akhaliq's 2.1 Next-Scene LoRA (Apache-2.0) lets Storyboard leave Qwen-Image-Edit 2509.

nm10-keying.brief:

In October Corridor Digital released CorridorKey 2.0 (native-resolution neural keying, linear EXR, 4-6 GB), ComfyUI-RMBG 3.3.0 brought Bria's VRMBG 3.0 (the same model Fuobe's cloud matte calls) and FeyNoBg hair matting to ComfyUI, and fal added Bria's green-screen despill and a guided cut-out that takes 'keep the shadow'.

Models (record licence, revision, size):
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). nm10-rtx-video.title: Instant upscale, HDR and frame generation on RTX cards with Comfy-Org's NVIDIA VFX nodes
nm10-rtx-video.brief:
WHY. Comfy-Org's ComfyUI Nvidia VFX Nodes 0.2.1 (2026-10-13) wrap NVIDIA's RTX Video SDK: super resolution up to 4x, SDR→HDR (HLG or PQ, 400-2000 nits) and frame generation up to 16x, all running in the GPU's dedicated paths in seconds, with an official 'RTX Video Enhance' template. Fuobe's quick tiers today are ESRGAN (no new detail), RIFE/FILM and a model-based SDR→HDR graph; this gives owners with RTX cards a near-instant option in three tools.
WHERE IT SHOWS UP. Upscale → Video ('Quick · RTX'), FPS boost ('RTX Frame Generation', RTX 40+), SDR to HDR ('RTX Video HDR'), the Canvas upscale node, and a fast preview tier that n7-3 and archive-restore can reuse.
Facts (github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_Nvidia_VFX_Nodes, v0.2.1; registry id comfyui_nvidia_rtx_nodes; formerly 'Nvidia RTX Nodes'; read the README and example workflows as data): nodes RTX Video Super Resolution (image/upscaling; IMAGE batch in, same frame count out; modes BICUBIC, LOW...ULTRA, DENOISE, DEBLUR, HIGHBITRATE, STREAMING; scale 1-4x or explicit size rounded to 8; chunks of <= 16 MP), RTX Video HDR (contrast, saturation, middle grey, peak 400-2000 nits, debanding; output BT.2020/HLG 'HDR' or BT.2020/PQ 'HDR PQ'; IMAGE carries no colour metadata, so the encoder must be told), RTX Video Frame Generation (2-16x or a single timestep; shot-change detection; output (N-1)M+1 frames; RTX 40 series or later). Requirements: NVIDIA RTX GPU, CUDA PyTorch cu130 or newer (check Fuobe's install script); no CPU or non-NVIDIA path. Licence: not stated on the page: read the repo LICENSE and NVIDIA's SDK terms and record them as information.

1. Pin the pack in workflows/comfyui/packs.json and install-comfyui.sh (only on NVIDIA hosts; the installer already knows the platform: skip elsewhere).
2. Graphs upscale-video-rtx (chunked the way upscale-video-esrgan-chunked is, sound kept), fps-rtx-framegen (multiplier or target fps; shot changes kept), sdr-to-hdr-rtx (HLG or PQ; encode HDR10 / ProRes with the right colour metadata, reusing the existing sdr-to-hdr export path). 3. Readiness: the tier needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU (and RTX 40+ for frame generation): /connect shows 'Needs an NVIDIA RTX card' otherwise; the chooser reads the GPU name from the status check.
4. Studios: 'Quick · RTX' first in Upscale → Video on eligible hosts (ESRGAN stays the fallback; SeedVR2 stays 'Restore · faithful'); FPS boost and SDR to HDR get the RTX choice beside RIFE/FILM and the current graph. Defaults: keep today's unless the owner chooses.
5. CLOUD: the SDK is not a hosted model: open-engine only; the cloud keeps Topaz / SeedVR / ByteDance upscalers under their own names.

nm10-kandinsky6.title: Kandinsky 6.0 on both engines: MIT-licensed 5 s clips with dialogue and sound, and Kandinsky VSR as an upscaler
nm10-kandinsky6.brief:
WHY. Kandinsky 6.0 Video (Kandinsky Lab, 2026-10-06, MIT) is the only new open video model with synchronised 44 kHz audio and lip-synced dialogue under a fully permissive licence, in a 29B Pro and a 3B Lite, with a first-party ComfyUI extension and the same models hosted on fal (Pro, Lite and the VSR upscaler). Round 4 judged it 'unproven vs Wan 2.2'; the Lite model is a sound-on option for smaller GPUs, and the VSR is the cheapest hosted video upscaler on fal ($0.08-0.09 for 5 s 480p→1080p).
WHERE IT SHOWS UP. Video studio model menu (both engines), Lipsync & avatars ('talking characters from words'), Upscale → Video ('Kandinsky VSR', both engines).
Facts (github.com/kandinskylab/kandinsky-6; kandinskylab/Kandinsky-6.0-Pro-distill-5s-Diffusers @ 80d5e6c7f646, MIT; read the README, the technical report and the ComfyUI extension as data): Pro 29B and Lite 3B, each as base, 10-step distilled (PiFlow, CFG 1) and pretrained checkpoints; 5 s clips at 24 fps (examples 480x864); 44 kHz synchronised audio (dialogue, ambience, music) with lip sync; modes T2AV and TI2AV (the image is the first frame); sample_audio False gives video only; expand_prompts rewrites short prompts (Qwen3.5-9B 'beautification', can be turned off). Architecture: Qwen2.5-VL embeddings + CLIP pooled, Hunyuan Video VAE, MMAudio VAE + BigVGAN vocoder, flow matching shift 5. Kandinsky6SRPipeline: x2, x2.25 or x4 by tiled diffusion in K-VAE latent space (4 steps per tile; the distilled VSR 2 steps), up to Full HD. ComfyUI: not native yet (core PR #16825 under review); first-party Registry packages kandinsky6 and kandinsky6-sr (ComfyUI >= 0.38; Fuobe pins 0.42.0), two templates (T2AV, TI2AV) defaulting to Pro distilled, MagCache supported (bypassed for distilled), a 'Download models' button. nm10-hy-nomas-world.title: World mode on your GPU: Hy-Nomas, a world you describe once and then steer turn by turn with words and camera moves
nm10-hy-nomas-world.brief:
WHY. 'Worlds' became a hot category in October: fal opened a worlds section (H3 Max Director, Abot World 0, Lingbot World 2, VAST Eden Live) and Tencent open-sourced Hy-Nomas (Apache-2.0, 2026-10-21), an interactive world model that keeps generating 720p video at 24 fps while you change the action in words and fly the camera on a trajectory. A community ComfyUI port loads it with stock loaders and measured ~21 s per 3 s turn on a 5090. Fuobe's Cinema already has camera paths (fly path) to drive it.
WHERE IT SHOWS UP. Cinema Studio: a 'World' take type (opening description, then turns with words and a camera move from the fly-path library), a turn timeline with redo, export as one film; Assist ('make a 60 s world walk-through').
Facts (tencent/Hy-Nomas @ bb6a8ca451bf, Apache-2.0 per the HF tag: read the LICENSE file and record it; github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Nomas; port github.com/Nynxz/ComfyUI-HyNomas with converted weights at huggingface.co/nynxz/Hy-Nomas; read all as data): 720x1280 at 24 fps; 8-step distilled config, Euler ODE, text and camera guidance 1.0; a JSON prompt file of segments (start/end times, a long opening description, short change descriptions for later turns, timed actions; inference.video_length=event derives lengths from event times); a trajectory file of camera-to-world matrices and intrinsics (trajectory_translation_scale 1.0, trajectory_rotation_scale 2.5 by default); keyboard/mouse control only in Tencent's hosted demo. The gallery example is 60 s from five 12 s text-only turns. Hardware: reference 8 GPUs with sequence parallelism; a single-4090 config uses INT8 DiT and KV cache, an FP8 decoder, stage-by-stage CPU offload and GPU history capped at 18 latent frames (speed unverified by Tencent); the port measured ~21 s per 3 s turn plus ~4 s decode per window on a 5090 at 1280x704 INT8. Files: DiT/distilled_int8 9.06 GB (port: INT8 DiT 9.0 GB in diffusion_models; BF16 17.1 GB for LoRA merges), PixelUMM VAE (31.55 GB in Tencent's repo; 15.8 GB converted by the port), a cinematic LoRA adapter 6.12 GB, the prompt enhancer PE (~55 GB, optional: offline inference reads prepared prompt files), the text encoder Qwen2.5-VL 7B loaded as type qwen_image from Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI (Fuobe may already pin it: check).
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there.
Build:
1. Pin the port (Nynxz/ComfyUI-HyNomas at a commit) and the converted weights in packs.json / model-pins.json; graph world-hy-nomas-turn: one turn = the previous turn's state (the port's history mechanism: read how it carries history between queue runs) + the turn's words + the turn's camera trajectory → 3-12 s of video; validate against the node list. If the port cannot carry history between separate /prompt calls, build the whole film as one graph with N turns and say so.
2. A pure, tested converter src/lib/world-path.ts: Fuobe's camera paths (scene3d keyframes / the fly-path library: orbits, dollies, trucks, figure-8) → Hy-Nomas camera-to-world matrices and intrinsics at 24 fps, with the default scales.
3. Cinema 'World' take: opening description, turns list (words + a camera move chip + seconds), Preview the path, Run turn, Redo from here (keeps earlier turns), Export (join with video-concat). Sound: Hy-Nomas makes none: offer the existing Foley / music tools after.
4. CLOUD: Hy-Nomas is not hosted on fal or Replicate: open engine only ('Runs on your GPU (open source)'; 'Paid APIs only' hides it). fal's worlds models (H3 Max Director realtime WebRTC sessions with a 60 s minimum; Abot World 0; Lingbot World 2 'research' licence; Eden Live) are different models, not stand-ins: record them in the research JSON; whether to offer any of them under its own name is the owner's call.
5. Relation to queued work: n7-9-worldcast-worker (WorldCast fly-around from one photo) is a different model and stays; reuse its camera-path pieces if they landed first.
6. /connect row: 'World mode' with the 24 GB+ (guess) requirement and the ~25 GB of files; licence row Apache-2.0 (and the PE and VAE licences as their cards say).
Tests: converter tests (matrix conventions, intrinsics, frame counts, scales), turn-state tests, library test, browser checks of the World take at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, in demo mode. No GPU here: every speed figure is the port author's.
CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED (the owner's rule): a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (the owner, 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does.

An account's run reads only its own files: it runs inside runAsTenant, src/server/tenant.ts says what work inside a tenant may use, and src/server/account-inputs.ts checks every input (input-not-allowed, input-not-yours, input-gone, input-too-big). A new server path that reads, fetches or chains a file for a run goes through them, with a test in the style of tests/account-tenant.test.ts and the other tests/account-*.test.ts. A price check (an estimate route, or ?preview=1 on a run route) goes in ESTIMATES or PREVIEWS and runs through priceAs (src/server/visitor.ts), so a visitor is priced for its own GPU on the open engine, never a demo. The sign-in proxy holds a request body only up to 4 MB (main, 10-31: proxyClientMaxBodySize in next.config.ts; a bigger body reaches the route cut short, with no error), so a route that takes a large file takes an uploaded file's reference instead (POST /api/uploads skips the proxy through src/server/direct-gate.ts). A route that must take a file itself skips the proxy the way main's do: the matcher in src/proxy.ts, then gateAsProxy and readBodyWithin or readFormWithin from src/server/direct-gate.ts, and a row in tests/request-body-limits.test.ts. Add each new route to those rules and to tests/public-signup.test.ts (tools in the style of tests/public-signup-tools.test.ts). A new ComfyUI workflow or node pack goes into the GPU pre-flight's requirement index (workflows/comfyui/packs.json and model-pins.json, then node scripts/comfy/build-requirements.mjs), and a new studio or tool gets a row on the pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS in src/server/gpu/tools.ts).

f1-h3-token-overage.title: MiniMax H3 reference tokens past 4,096 are priced
f1-h3-token-overage.brief:
WHY. The owner, 11-04. nm10-hosted-catchup left reference-token overage unpriced: H3 insert at $0.02 per 1K tokens and H3 Max Turbo references at $0.016 per 1K past 4,096 tokens are only mentioned in the price notes, so a shown price can be lower than the bill.
ACTION. Check the overage rates and how fal counts reference tokens at the source. Add the overage to the price (src/lib/catalog/plan.ts estimateCost, a Pricing rule in src/lib/catalog/types.ts as kling-4's clipInput did) wherever the count is known before the run (prompt length, reference count and sizes); where it can only be known after, price the minimum and say what can be added, in plain words. The price shown before a run never undercounts what fal bills for the inputs given. Tests for each route's price at, below and above 4,096 tokens.
